# Page: Model Architecture

# Model Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md](.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md)
- [deepspot/cell/model.py](deepspot/cell/model.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides an in-depth overview of the neural network architecture shared by both `DeepCell` and `DeepSpot` models. It covers the two-stage Phi-Rho ensemble design, context modes for handling spatial relationships, and the training lifecycle. For detailed documentation of individual model classes, see [DeepCell Model](#5.1) and [DeepSpot Model](#5.2). For the underlying neural layer implementations, see [Phi and Rho Neural Layers](#5.3). For optimization objectives, see [Loss Functions](#5.4).

---

## Architectural Overview

Both `DeepCell` and `DeepSpot` implement a two-stage ensemble architecture consisting of **Phi modules** for feature transformation and **Rho modules** for final prediction. This design follows a deep-set architecture pattern that enables the models to process variable-sized inputs (e.g., spots with different numbers of sub-tiles or neighbors) while maintaining permutation invariance.

### Two-Stage Ensemble Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input Features<br/>(Foundation Model Embeddings)"]
    
    subgraph PhiStage["Phi Stage: Feature Transformation"]
        Phi1["Phi Module 1<br/>Linear → Dropout → ReLU"]
        Phi2["Phi Module 2<br/>Linear → Dropout → ReLU"]
        PhiN["Phi Module 10<br/>Linear → Dropout → ReLU"]
        MedianAgg["Median Aggregation"]
        
        Phi1 --> MedianAgg
        Phi2 --> MedianAgg
        PhiN --> MedianAgg
    end
    
    subgraph RhoStage["Rho Stage: Gene Expression Prediction"]
        Rho1["Rho Module 1<br/>Dropout → ReLU → Linear"]
        Rho2["Rho Module 2<br/>Dropout → ReLU → Linear"]
        RhoN["Rho Module 10<br/>Dropout → ReLU → Linear"]
        MeanAgg["Mean Aggregation"]
        
        Rho1 --> MeanAgg
        Rho2 --> MeanAgg
        RhoN --> MeanAgg
    end
    
    Input --> Phi1
    Input --> Phi2
    Input --> PhiN
    
    MedianAgg --> Rho1
    MedianAgg --> Rho2
    MedianAgg --> RhoN
    
    MeanAgg --> Output["Gene Expression Predictions<br/>(output_size genes)"]
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-60](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:125-127](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-214]()

### Key Architectural Properties

| Component | Purpose | Aggregation | Count |
|-----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| **Phi Modules** | Transform input features to intermediate representation | Median across ensemble | 10 (default, configurable via `n_ensemble_phi`) |
| **Rho Modules** | Transform Phi output to gene expression predictions | Mean across ensemble | 10 (default, configurable via `n_ensemble_rho`) |
| **Input Size** | Foundation model embedding dimension | N/A | 1024 (UNI), 1536 (Hoptimus0), 768 (Phikon), 2048 (Inception) |
| **Phi Output** | Intermediate representation dimension | N/A | 1024 (default, configurable via `phi2rho_size`) |
| **Output Size** | Number of genes to predict | N/A | 300-800 (Visium), 500 (Xenium) |

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:64-81]()

---

## Model Variants and Context Modes

The architecture supports two model variants operating at different spatial resolutions, each with multiple context modes for incorporating spatial information.

### DeepSpot Context Modes

```mermaid
graph TB
    DeepSpot["DeepSpot Model"]
    
    subgraph SpotContexts["Spot Context Modes"]
        Spot["spot<br/>Single spot features<br/>phi_multiplier=1"]
        SpotSubspot["spot_subspot<br/>Spot + 9 mini-tiles<br/>phi_multiplier=2"]
        SpotNeighbors["spot_neighbors<br/>Spot + neighbor spots<br/>phi_multiplier=2"]
        SpotSubspotNeighbors["spot_subspot_neighbors<br/>Full context<br/>phi_multiplier=3"]
    end
    
    ForwardSpot["_forward_spot()"]
    ForwardSpotSubspot["_forward_spot_subspot()"]
    ForwardSpotNeighbors["_forward_spot_neighbors()"]
    ForwardSpotSubspotNeighbors["_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors()"]
    
    DeepSpot -->|spot_context='spot'| Spot
    DeepSpot -->|spot_context='spot_subspot'| SpotSubspot
    DeepSpot -->|spot_context='spot_neighbors'| SpotNeighbors
    DeepSpot -->|spot_context='spot_subspot_neighbors'| SpotSubspotNeighbors
    
    Spot --> ForwardSpot
    SpotSubspot --> ForwardSpotSubspot
    SpotNeighbors --> ForwardSpotNeighbors
    SpotSubspotNeighbors --> ForwardSpotSubspotNeighbors
    
    ForwardSpot --> PhiRho["Phi-Rho Pipeline"]
    ForwardSpotSubspot --> PhiRho
    ForwardSpotNeighbors --> PhiRho
    ForwardSpotSubspotNeighbors --> PhiRho
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-126](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-187]()

### DeepCell Context Modes

```mermaid
graph TB
    DeepCell["DeepCell Model"]
    
    subgraph CellContexts["Cell Context Modes"]
        Cell["cell<br/>Single cell features<br/>phi_multiplier=1"]
        CellNeighbors["cell_neighbors<br/>Cell + neighbor cells<br/>phi_multiplier=2"]
    end
    
    ForwardCell["_forward_cell()"]
    ForwardCellNeighbors["_forward_cell_neighbors()"]
    
    DeepCell -->|cell_context='cell'| Cell
    DeepCell -->|cell_context='cell_neighbors'| CellNeighbors
    
    Cell --> ForwardCell
    CellNeighbors --> ForwardCellNeighbors
    
    ForwardCell --> PhiRho["Phi-Rho Pipeline"]
    ForwardCellNeighbors --> PhiRho
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:130-142](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:179-188]()

### Context Mode Comparison

| Model | Context Mode | Description | Phi Multiplier | Forward Function |
|-------|--------------|-------------|----------------|------------------|
| **DeepSpot** | `spot` | Individual spot only | 1 | `_forward_spot()` |
| **DeepSpot** | `spot_subspot` | Spot + 9 mini-tiles (3×3 grid) | 2 | `_forward_spot_subspot()` |
| **DeepSpot** | `spot_neighbors` | Spot + neighboring spots | 2 | `_forward_spot_neighbors()` |
| **DeepSpot** | `spot_subspot_neighbors` | Spot + mini-tiles + neighbors (full) | 3 | `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors()` |
| **DeepCell** | `cell` | Individual cell only | 1 | `_forward_cell()` |
| **DeepCell** | `cell_neighbors` | Cell + neighboring cells | 2 | `_forward_cell_neighbors()` |

The `phi_multiplier` determines the input dimension to Rho modules: `phi2rho_size × phi_multiplier`. This accommodates concatenated Phi outputs from multiple spatial contexts.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:130-135](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-117]()

---

## Component-Level Architecture

### Phi Module Design

The `Phi` class implements feature transformation with the following structure:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Input<br/>(batch × input_size)"]
    Linear["Linear Layer<br/>(input_size → output_size)"]
    Dropout["Dropout<br/>(p=p_phi)"]
    ReLU["ReLU Activation<br/>(inplace=True)"]
    Output["Output<br/>(batch × output_size)"]
    
    Input --> Linear
    Linear --> Dropout
    Dropout --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Output
```

**Implementation Details:**
- **Input Size**: Foundation model embedding dimension (e.g., 1024 for UNI)
- **Output Size**: Configurable via `phi2rho_size` parameter (default: 1024)
- **Dropout Rate**: Configurable via `p_phi` parameter (default: 0.2)
- **Activation**: ReLU with in-place operation for memory efficiency

**Ensemble Aggregation:**
For each input, all Phi modules in the ensemble process it independently. The median value across the ensemble is selected for each feature dimension, providing robustness to outlier predictions.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-46](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-209]()

### Rho Module Design

The `Rho` class implements final gene expression prediction:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Input<br/>(batch × phi2rho_size × phi_multiplier)"]
    Dropout1["Dropout<br/>(p=p_rho)"]
    ReLU["ReLU Activation<br/>(inplace=True)"]
    Linear["Linear Layer<br/>(phi2rho_size × phi_multiplier → output_size)"]
    Dropout2["Dropout<br/>(p=0.1)"]
    Output["Output<br/>(batch × output_size)"]
    
    Input --> Dropout1
    Dropout1 --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Linear
    Linear --> Dropout2
    Dropout2 --> Output
```

**Implementation Details:**
- **Input Size**: `phi2rho_size × phi_multiplier` (e.g., 1024×2 = 2048 for `cell_neighbors` mode)
- **Output Size**: Number of genes to predict (e.g., 500 for Xenium)
- **Dropout Rates**: Configurable `p_rho` before activation (default: 0.2), fixed 0.1 after linear layer
- **Activation**: ReLU with in-place operation

**Ensemble Aggregation:**
The mean of all Rho module outputs is computed, providing a stable final prediction by averaging over the ensemble.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:49-60](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:211-214]()

---

## Forward Pass Mechanisms

### Spatial Context Processing

Different context modes process spatial information differently through the Phi-Rho pipeline:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph CellOnly["Cell-Only Forward (_forward_cell)"]
        C_Input["x: cell features<br/>(batch × 1 × input_size)"]
        C_Phi["Apply Phi<br/>(no aggregation)"]
        C_Rho["Apply Rho"]
        C_Output["predictions"]
        
        C_Input --> C_Phi
        C_Phi --> C_Rho
        C_Rho --> C_Output
    end
    
    subgraph CellNeighbors["Cell + Neighbors Forward (_forward_cell_neighbors)"]
        CN_Input["x: [cell, neighbors]<br/>cell: (batch × 1 × input_size)<br/>neighbors: (batch × n_neighbors × input_size)"]
        CN_PhiCell["Apply Phi to cell<br/>(no aggregation)"]
        CN_PhiNeigh["Apply Phi to neighbors<br/>(max/mean/sum aggregation)"]
        CN_Concat["Concatenate<br/>(batch × phi2rho_size × 2)"]
        CN_Rho["Apply Rho"]
        CN_Output["predictions"]
        
        CN_Input --> CN_PhiCell
        CN_Input --> CN_PhiNeigh
        CN_PhiCell --> CN_Concat
        CN_PhiNeigh --> CN_Concat
        CN_Concat --> CN_Rho
        CN_Rho --> CN_Output
    end
```

**Neighbor Aggregation Strategies:**
The `agg_neighbors` parameter (default: `"max"`) controls how neighbor features are aggregated after Phi transformation:
- **`max`**: Takes maximum value across neighbors for each feature dimension
- **`mean`**: Computes mean across neighbors
- **`sum`**: Sums neighbor features

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:179-188](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:109-115]()

### Spot Context Processing

DeepSpot extends this pattern to support sub-spot tiles:

| Forward Function | Inputs | Phi Applications | Concatenation |
|------------------|--------|-----------------|---------------|
| `_forward_spot()` | `x` (spot features) | Spot through `phi_spot` | Single Phi output |
| `_forward_spot_subspot()` | `[x_spot, x_subspot]` | Spot through `phi_spot`, subspots through `phi_subspot` | 2 Phi outputs |
| `_forward_spot_neighbors()` | `[x_spot, x_neighbors]` | Spot through `phi_spot`, neighbors through `phi_spot` (aggregated) | 2 Phi outputs |
| `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors()` | `[x_spot, x_subspot, x_neighbors]` | Spot through `phi_spot`, subspots through `phi_subspot`, neighbors through `phi_spot` (aggregated) | 3 Phi outputs |

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-187]()

---

## Training Lifecycle

Both models inherit from `lightning.LightningModule` and implement standard PyTorch Lightning training patterns:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Init["__init__()<br/>Initialize Phi/Rho ensembles<br/>Configure loss function<br/>Set hyperparameters"]
    
    TrainStep["training_step(batch, batch_idx)<br/>→ loop_step(batch, 'train')"]
    ValStep["validation_step(batch, batch_idx)<br/>→ loop_step(batch, 'val')"]
    
    LoopStep["loop_step(batch, stage)"]
    Forward["forward(X)<br/>→ _forward_fn(X)"]
    Loss["loss_func(y_hat, y)"]
    Log["Log metrics<br/>self.log(stage, loss)"]
    
    Optimizer["configure_optimizers()<br/>AdamW optimizer"]
    
    Init --> TrainStep
    Init --> ValStep
    Init --> Optimizer
    
    TrainStep --> LoopStep
    ValStep --> LoopStep
    
    LoopStep --> Forward
    Forward --> Loss
    Loss --> Log
    
    Log -->|accumulate| TrainingLoss["self.training_loss[]"]
    Log -->|accumulate| ValidationLoss["self.validation_loss[]"]
    
    TrainingLoss --> PlotLoss["plot_loss()<br/>Visualize training curves"]
    ValidationLoss --> PlotLoss
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:144-168](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:235-281]()

### Key Training Components

| Component | Implementation | Configuration |
|-----------|----------------|---------------|
| **Optimizer** | `torch.optim.AdamW` | `lr` (default: 1e-4), `weight_decay` (default: 1e-6) |
| **Loss Function** | Configurable via `loss_func` parameter | See [Loss Functions](#5.4) for available options |
| **Loss Tracking** | `self.training_loss` and `self.validation_loss` lists | Populated during `loop_step()` |
| **Visualization** | `plot_loss()` method | Exponentially smoothed training curves with original overlays |
| **Random Seed** | `fix_seed(random_seed)` | Ensures reproducibility (default: 2024) |

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:64-81](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218]()

# Core architecture parameters
input_size: int           # Foundation model embedding dimension
output_size: int          # Number of genes to predict
phi2rho_size: int = 1024  # Intermediate representation size
emb_size: int = 1024      # (Deprecated, maintained for compatibility)

# Ensemble configuration
n_ensemble: int = 10           # Default ensemble size
n_ensemble_phi: int = None     # Phi ensemble size (defaults to n_ensemble)
n_ensemble_rho: int = None     # Rho ensemble size (defaults to n_ensemble)

# Regularization
p: float = 0.2                 # Default dropout probability
p_phi: float = None            # Phi dropout (defaults to p)
p_rho: float = None            # Rho dropout (defaults to p)

# Training configuration
loss_func: str = "mse"         # Loss function identifier
lr: float = 1e-4               # Learning rate
weight_decay: float = 1e-6     # AdamW weight decay
random_seed: int = 2024        # Random seed for reproducibility

# Data processing
scaler = None                  # Optional scaler for inverse transforms
```

```

---

## Summary

The DeepSpot architecture implements a flexible two-stage ensemble design that supports multiple spatial context modes for both spot-level and cell-level spatial transcriptomics prediction:

- **Phi Stage**: Transforms input features through 10 parallel modules with median aggregation for robustness
- **Rho Stage**: Generates final predictions through 10 parallel modules with mean aggregation for stability
- **Context Modes**: Enable incorporation of spatial relationships (sub-tiles, neighbors) while maintaining a unified architecture
- **Training**: Leverages PyTorch Lightning for standardized training loops with configurable loss functions and AdamW optimization

For implementation details of specific model variants, see [DeepCell Model](#5.1) and [DeepSpot Model](#5.2). For neural layer internals, see [Phi and Rho Neural Layers](#5.3). For optimization objectives, see [Loss Functions](#5.4).

---

## Purpose and Scope

The `DeepCell` model is the core neural network architecture for predicting gene expression at single-cell resolution from H&E histology images. This page documents the `DeepCell` class implementation, including its initialization parameters, cell context modes, forward pass mechanisms, and training lifecycle.

For information about the underlying Phi and Rho neural layer implementations, see [Phi and Rho Neural Layers](#5.3). For details about available loss functions, see [Loss Functions](#5.4). For the spot-level equivalent model, see [DeepSpot Model](#5.2).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:63-281]()

---

## Class Overview

The `DeepCell` class inherits from `lightning.LightningModule`, leveraging PyTorch Lightning's training orchestration capabilities. The model implements a deep-set architecture that processes cell-level histology features and optionally incorporates spatial neighbor information to predict gene expression profiles.

```mermaid
graph TB
    LightningModule["lightning.LightningModule<br/>(PyTorch Lightning)"]
    DeepCell["DeepCell<br/>deepspot.cell.model.DeepCell"]
    
    PhiModules["phi_cell: nn.ModuleList<br/>(n_ensemble_phi instances)"]
    RhoModules["rho: nn.ModuleList<br/>(n_ensemble_rho instances)"]
    LossFunc["loss_func<br/>(selected from deepspot.cell.loss)"]
    
    LightningModule -->|"inherits from"| DeepCell
    DeepCell -->|"initializes"| PhiModules
    DeepCell -->|"initializes"| RhoModules
    DeepCell -->|"configures"| LossFunc
    
    PhiModules -.->|"feature transformation"| RhoModules
    RhoModules -.->|"gene expression output"| Predictions["Predicted Gene Counts"]
```

**Core Responsibilities:**
- Initialize ensemble of Phi and Rho neural network modules
- Configure loss function and optimizer
- Execute forward passes based on cell context mode
- Track training and validation losses
- Provide loss visualization capabilities

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:63-128]()

---

## Initialization Parameters

The `DeepCell.__init__` method accepts the following parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_size` | `int` | - | Dimension of input feature vectors (foundation model output) |
| `output_size` | `int` | - | Number of genes to predict |
| `loss_func` | `str` | `"mse"` | Loss function identifier: `"mse"`, `"cos"`, `"l1"`, `"huber"`, `"mse_cos"`, `"l1_cos"`, `"huber_cos"`, `"pearson"`, `"mse_pearson"`, `"poisson"` |
| `lr` | `float` | `1e-4` | Learning rate for AdamW optimizer |
| `p` | `float` | `0.2` | Default dropout probability for Phi and Rho |
| `p_phi` | `Union[None, float]` | `None` | Dropout probability for Phi layers (overrides `p` if set) |
| `p_rho` | `Union[None, float]` | `None` | Dropout probability for Rho layers (overrides `p` if set) |
| `n_ensemble` | `int` | `10` | Default number of ensemble models |
| `n_ensemble_phi` | `Union[None, int]` | `None` | Number of Phi ensemble models (overrides `n_ensemble` if set) |
| `n_ensemble_rho` | `Union[None, int]` | `None` | Number of Rho ensemble models (overrides `n_ensemble` if set) |
| `phi2rho_size` | `int` | `1024` | Dimension of Phi output / Rho input |
| `emb_size` | `int` | `1024` | Embedding size (stored but not actively used) |
| `weight_decay` | `float` | `1e-6` | L2 regularization weight for AdamW |
| `random_seed` | `int` | `2024` | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `agg_neighbors` | `str` | `"max"` | Aggregation operation for neighbor features: `"max"`, `"mean"`, `"sum"` |
| `scaler` | - | `None` | Optional scaler object for inverse transformation |
| `cell_context` | `str` | `"cell_neighbors"` | Forward pass mode: `"cell"` or `"cell_neighbors"` |

**Loss Function Mapping:**

The `loss_func` parameter maps to functions in [deepspot/cell/loss.py]():

```mermaid
graph LR
    mse["loss_func='mse'"]
    cos["loss_func='cos'"]
    l1["loss_func='l1'"]
    huber["loss_func='huber'"]
    mse_cos["loss_func='mse_cos'"]
    l1_cos["loss_func='l1_cos'"]
    huber_cos["loss_func='huber_cos'"]
    pearson["loss_func='pearson'"]
    mse_pearson["loss_func='mse_pearson'"]
    poisson["loss_func='poisson'"]
    
    mse -->|"assigns"| loss_mse_function
    cos -->|"assigns"| loss_cosine_function
    l1 -->|"assigns"| loss_l1_function
    huber -->|"assigns"| loss_huber_function
    mse_cos -->|"assigns"| loss_mse_cosine_function
    l1_cos -->|"assigns"| loss_l1_cosine_function
    huber_cos -->|"assigns"| loss_huber_cosine_function
    pearson -->|"assigns"| loss_pearson_function
    mse_pearson -->|"assigns"| loss_mse_pearson_function
    poisson -->|"assigns"| loss_poisson_function
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:64-128](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]()

## Cell Context Modes

The `cell_context` parameter determines which forward pass function is used. The model supports two modes:

### Mode Comparison

| Mode | Forward Function | Input Structure | Phi Multiplier | Description |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|-------------|
| `"cell"` | `_forward_cell` | Single tensor | 1 | Processes individual cell features only |
| `"cell_neighbors"` | `_forward_cell_neighbors` | List of 2 tensors | 2 | Processes cell + aggregated neighbor features |

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "cell_context='cell'"
        CellInput["x: torch.Tensor<br/>(batch_size, 1, input_size)"]
        CellPhi["_apply_phi(x, phi_cell,<br/>operation=NONE)"]
        CellRho["_apply_rho(x_phi)"]
        CellOutput["output: torch.Tensor<br/>(batch_size, output_size)"]
        
        CellInput --> CellPhi
        CellPhi --> CellRho
        CellRho --> CellOutput
    end
    
    subgraph "cell_context='cell_neighbors'"
        NeighInput["x: List[torch.Tensor]<br/>[x_cell, x_neighbors]"]
        NeighCellPhi["_apply_phi(x_cell, phi_cell,<br/>operation=NONE)"]
        NeighNeighPhi["_apply_phi(x_neighbors, phi_cell,<br/>operation=agg_neighbors)"]
        Concat["torch.cat((x_cell, x_neighbors),<br/>dim=1)"]
        NeighRho["_apply_rho(x_phi)"]
        NeighOutput["output: torch.Tensor<br/>(batch_size, output_size)"]
        
        NeighInput --> NeighCellPhi
        NeighInput --> NeighNeighPhi
        NeighCellPhi --> Concat
        NeighNeighPhi --> Concat
        Concat --> NeighRho
        NeighRho --> NeighOutput
    end
```

**Phi Multiplier Impact:**

The `_get_phi_multiplier` method determines the Rho input size based on context:
- `"cell"`: multiplier = 1 → Rho input = `phi2rho_size`
- `"cell_neighbors"`: multiplier = 2 → Rho input = `2 * phi2rho_size`

This is because in `"cell_neighbors"` mode, the cell and neighbor Phi outputs are concatenated before passing to Rho.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:130-142](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:179-188]()

---

## Forward Pass Mechanisms

### Overview of Forward Execution

The `forward` method delegates to the appropriate forward function based on the `cell_context` configuration:

```mermaid
graph TB
    ForwardCall["forward(x)"]
    CheckContext{"self._forward_fn<br/>(set during __init__)"}
    
    ForwardCell["_forward_cell(x)"]
    ForwardCellNeighbors["_forward_cell_neighbors(x)"]
    
    ForwardCall --> CheckContext
    CheckContext -->|"cell_context='cell'"| ForwardCell
    CheckContext -->|"cell_context='cell_neighbors'"| ForwardCellNeighbors
```

### _forward_cell

Processes individual cell features without neighbor information:

1. Apply Phi ensemble to cell features (no aggregation)
2. Apply Rho ensemble to transformed features
3. Return predicted gene expression

**Implementation:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:179-181]()

### _forward_cell_neighbors

Processes cell features with neighbor context:

1. Split input into `x_cell` and `x_neighbors`
2. Apply Phi ensemble to `x_cell` (no aggregation)
3. Apply Phi ensemble to `x_neighbors` (aggregate across neighbors using `agg_neighbors` operation)
4. Concatenate transformed cell and neighbor features
5. Apply Rho ensemble to concatenated features
6. Return predicted gene expression

**Implementation:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:183-188]()

### _apply_phi

Core Phi transformation with ensemble and optional aggregation:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["x: (batch_size, sample_size, input_size)"]
    Reshape1["Reshape to (-1, input_size)"]
    PhiEnsemble["Apply n_ensemble_phi Phi modules"]
    MedianAgg["Median aggregation across ensemble"]
    Reshape2["Reshape to (batch_size, sample_size, phi2rho_size)"]
    
    CheckOp{"operation type?"}
    OpSum["Sum across sample_size"]
    OpMean["Mean across sample_size"]
    OpMax["Max across sample_size"]
    OpNone["Flatten to (batch_size, sample_size * phi2rho_size)"]
    
    Output["x_phi"]
    
    Input --> Reshape1
    Reshape1 --> PhiEnsemble
    PhiEnsemble --> MedianAgg
    MedianAgg --> Reshape2
    Reshape2 --> CheckOp
    
    CheckOp -->|"SUM"| OpSum
    CheckOp -->|"MEAN"| OpMean
    CheckOp -->|"MAX"| OpMax
    CheckOp -->|"NONE"| OpNone
    
    OpSum --> Output
    OpMean --> Output
    OpMax --> Output
    OpNone --> Output
```

**Key Behavior:**
- Applies each Phi module independently to all samples
- Uses **median aggregation** across the ensemble (robust to outliers)
- `Operation.NONE`: Used for target cell features (preserves spatial structure before Rho)
- `Operation.MAX/MEAN/SUM`: Used for neighbor aggregation

**Implementation:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-209]()

### _apply_rho

Final gene expression prediction with ensemble averaging:

1. Apply each Rho module independently to Phi-transformed features
2. **Mean aggregation** across ensemble (smooth predictions)
3. Return final gene expression predictions

**Implementation:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:211-214]()

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:170-214]()

---

## Neighbor Aggregation Operations

The `agg_neighbors` parameter controls how neighbor features are combined in `_forward_cell_neighbors` mode. The `Operation` enum defines available operations:

```mermaid
graph LR
    OpEnum["Operation (Enum)"]
    OpSum["SUM = 'sum'<br/>Sum all neighbor features"]
    OpMax["MAX = 'max'<br/>Max pooling across neighbors"]
    OpMean["MEAN = 'mean'<br/>Average neighbor features"]
    OpNone["NONE = 'none'<br/>No aggregation (flatten)"]
    
    OpEnum --> OpSum
    OpEnum --> OpMax
    OpEnum --> OpMean
    OpEnum --> OpNone
```

| Operation | Behavior | Use Case |
|-----------|----------|----------|
| `MAX` | Takes maximum value across neighbors for each feature dimension | Default; captures strongest signals from neighborhood |
| `MEAN` | Averages neighbor features | Smooth representation of neighborhood |
| `SUM` | Sums neighbor features | Accumulates total neighborhood signal |
| `NONE` | Flattens all features without aggregation | Not typically used for neighbors |

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:29-33](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:109-114]()

---

## Training Lifecycle

### Training and Validation Steps

The model implements PyTorch Lightning's training interface:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Trainer["Lightning Trainer"]
    
    TrainingStep["training_step(batch, batch_idx)"]
    ValidationStep["validation_step(batch, batch_idx)"]
    LoopStep["loop_step(batch, stage)"]
    
    Forward["self(X)"]
    LossCalc["loss_func(y_hat, y)"]
    Logging["self.log(stage, loss)"]
    Tracking["Append to training_loss or validation_loss"]
    
    Trainer -->|"calls"| TrainingStep
    Trainer -->|"calls"| ValidationStep
    
    TrainingStep -->|"stage='train'"| LoopStep
    ValidationStep -->|"stage='val'"| LoopStep
    
    LoopStep --> Forward
    Forward --> LossCalc
    LossCalc --> Logging
    LossCalc --> Tracking
```

**loop_step Method:**

1. Unpack batch into features `X` and targets `y`
2. Convert to float tensors (handle list inputs for neighbor mode)
3. Execute forward pass: `y_hat = self(X)`
4. Compute loss: `loss = self.loss_func(y_hat, y)`
5. Log loss to Lightning logger with stage prefix
6. Track loss in `self.training_loss` or `self.validation_loss` list
7. Return loss for backpropagation

**Implementation:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:144-168]()

### Loss Tracking

The model maintains two lists for monitoring training progress:

- `self.training_loss`: List of loss values from each training batch
- `self.validation_loss`: List of loss values from each validation batch

These lists are populated during `loop_step` and used by the `plot_loss` method for visualization.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:121-122](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:157-160]()

---

## Optimizer Configuration

The model uses AdamW optimizer with L2 weight decay:

```python
# From deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218
def configure_optimizers(self) -> dict:
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        self.parameters(), 
        lr=self.hparams.lr,           # Default: 1e-4
        weight_decay=self.hparams.weight_decay  # Default: 1e-6
    )
    return {"optimizer": optimizer}
```

**Configuration:**
- **Optimizer:** `torch.optim.AdamW`
- **Learning Rate:** Configured via `lr` parameter (default: `1e-4`)
- **Weight Decay:** Configured via `weight_decay` parameter (default: `1e-6`)
- **No Learning Rate Scheduler:** Simple constant learning rate

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218]()

---

## Loss Visualization

### plot_loss Method

The `plot_loss` method provides visualization of training progress with exponential smoothing:

**Visualization Pipeline:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    TrainLoss["self.training_loss<br/>(per batch)"]
    ValLoss["self.validation_loss<br/>(per validation interval)"]
    
    Interpolate["Interpolate validation loss<br/>to training batch frequency"]
    Smooth["Apply exponential smoothing<br/>(alpha=0.2)"]
    
    Plot["matplotlib plot:<br/>- Original losses (transparent)<br/>- Smoothed losses (solid)"]
    
    TrainLoss --> Smooth
    ValLoss --> Interpolate
    Interpolate --> Smooth
    Smooth --> Plot
```

**Features:**

1. **Exponential Smoothing:** Applies `smooth_curve` method with `alpha=0.2` to reduce noise
2. **Validation Loss Interpolation:** Validation loss is recorded less frequently than training loss, so it's interpolated to match training step count
3. **Dual Plotting:** Shows both original (transparent) and smoothed (solid) curves
4. **Color Coding:** Blue for training loss, orange for validation loss

**smooth_curve Method:**

Uses exponential weighted moving average:
```
smoothed[0] = data[0]
smoothed[i] = alpha * data[i] + (1 - alpha) * smoothed[i-1]
```

With `alpha=0.2`, each point is 20% current value and 80% smoothed previous value.

**Implementation:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:220-281]()

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:220-281]()

---

## Inverse Transformation

The `inverse_transform` method applies inverse scaling if a scaler was provided during initialization:

```python
# From deepspot/cell/model.py:174-177
def inverse_transform(self, x) -> torch.Tensor:
    if self.scaler is not None:
        x = self.scaler.inverse_transform(x)
    return x
```

This is typically used to convert normalized/scaled predictions back to original gene expression scales. The scaler object should implement an `inverse_transform` method compatible with the data preprocessing pipeline.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:174-177]()

---

## Ensemble Architecture Summary

The `DeepCell` model uses a two-stage ensemble architecture:

| Stage | Module | Count | Aggregation | Purpose |
|-------|--------|-------|-------------|---------|
| Phi | `phi_cell` | `n_ensemble_phi` (default: 10) | **Median** | Feature transformation with robustness to outliers |
| Rho | `rho` | `n_ensemble_rho` (default: 10) | **Mean** | Gene expression prediction with smoothed outputs |

**Ensemble Benefits:**
- **Median aggregation (Phi):** Reduces impact of individual module failures or extreme transformations
- **Mean aggregation (Rho):** Produces smooth, averaged predictions across ensemble members
- **Independent training:** Each ensemble member learns slightly different feature representations due to dropout

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:125-127](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:195-196](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:212-213]()

---

## Complete Data Flow Example

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Stage"
        BatchData["Batch from DeepCellDataLoader"]
        XCell["x_cell: (batch_size, 1, input_size)"]
        XNeigh["x_neighbors: (batch_size, num_neighbors, input_size)"]
        Y["y: (batch_size, output_size)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Forward Pass: _forward_cell_neighbors"
        PhiCell["Phi ensemble on x_cell<br/>Median aggregation<br/>→ (batch_size, phi2rho_size)"]
        PhiNeigh["Phi ensemble on x_neighbors<br/>Median then MAX/MEAN/SUM<br/>→ (batch_size, phi2rho_size)"]
        Concat["Concatenate<br/>→ (batch_size, 2*phi2rho_size)"]
        RhoEns["Rho ensemble<br/>Mean aggregation<br/>→ (batch_size, output_size)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Loss & Optimization"
        LossCalc["loss_func(y_hat, y)"]
        Backward["Backpropagation"]
        AdamW["AdamW.step()"]
    end
    
    BatchData --> XCell
    BatchData --> XNeigh
    BatchData --> Y
    
    XCell --> PhiCell
    XNeigh --> PhiNeigh
    PhiCell --> Concat
    PhiNeigh --> Concat
    Concat --> RhoEns
    
    RhoEns --> LossCalc
    Y --> LossCalc
    LossCalc --> Backward
    Backward --> AdamW
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:63-218]()

# Page: DeepSpot Model

# DeepSpot Model

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md](.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md)
- [deepspot/cell/model.py](deepspot/cell/model.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the `DeepSpot` model class, which implements spot-level spatial transcriptomics prediction for Visium data (~55μm resolution). The model predicts gene expression profiles from H&E image features extracted at spot locations. For cell-level predictions on Xenium data, see [DeepCell Model](#5.1). For details on the Phi and Rho neural layer implementations, see [Phi and Rho Neural Layers](#5.3). For loss function details, see [Loss Functions](#5.4).

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:58-217](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:43-62]()

---

## Class Overview

The `DeepSpot` class ([deepspot/spot/model.py:58-217]()) is a PyTorch Lightning module (`L.LightningModule`) that implements a deep-set architecture for predicting gene expression from spot-level morphological features. The model supports four distinct spatial context modes that incorporate varying levels of sub-spot detail and neighborhood information.

### Key Characteristics

| Characteristic | Description |
|---|---|
| **Base Class** | `lightning.LightningModule` |
| **Primary Purpose** | Spot-level gene expression prediction |
| **Spatial Contexts** | 4 modes: `spot`, `spot_subspot`, `spot_neighbors`, `spot_subspot_neighbors` |
| **Architecture Pattern** | Deep-set with Phi (feature transformation) and Rho (aggregation) ensembles |
| **Loss Functions** | MSE, Pearson, Cosine, L1, Huber, Poisson, and combinations |
| **Optimizer** | AdamW with configurable learning rate and weight decay |

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:58-217](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:43-62]()

---

## Initialization Parameters

The `DeepSpot.__init__` method ([deepspot/spot/model.py:59-108]()) accepts the following configuration parameters:

### Core Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input_size` | `int` | Required | Dimensionality of input features (e.g., 1024 for UNI, 1536 for Hoptimus0) |
| `output_size` | `int` | Required | Number of genes to predict (e.g., 300-800 HVGs) |
| `loss_func` | `str` | `"mse"` | Loss function identifier: `"mse"`, `"pearson"`, `"cos"`, `"l1"`, `"huber"`, `"poisson"`, `"mse_pearson"`, `"mse_cos"`, `"l1_cos"`, `"huber_cos"` |
| `lr` | `float` | `1e-4` | Learning rate for AdamW optimizer |

### Ensemble Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_ensemble` | `int` | `10` | Number of parallel networks in both Phi and Rho ensembles |
| `n_ensemble_phi` | `int \| None` | `None` | Override for Phi ensemble size (defaults to `n_ensemble`) |
| `n_ensemble_rho` | `int \| None` | `None` | Override for Rho ensemble size (defaults to `n_ensemble`) |
| `phi2rho_size` | `int` | `1024` | Intermediate feature dimension between Phi and Rho stages |

### Regularization Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `p` | `float` | `0.2` | Dropout probability for both Phi and Rho layers |
| `p_phi` | `float \| None` | `None` | Override dropout for Phi layers (defaults to `p`) |
| `p_rho` | `float \| None` | `None` | Override dropout for Rho layers (defaults to `p`) |
| `weight_decay` | `float` | `1e-6` | L2 regularization coefficient for AdamW |

### Context and Utility Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spot_context` | `str` | `"spot_subspot_neighbors"` | Spatial context mode (see below) |
| `agg_neighbors` | `str` | `"max"` | Neighborhood aggregation: `"max"`, `"mean"`, or `"sum"` |
| `random_seed` | `int` | `2024` | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `scaler` | `object \| None` | `None` | Scikit-learn scaler for inverse transformation |

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:59-108]()

---

## Spot Context Modes

The `DeepSpot` model supports four distinct spatial context modes configured via the `spot_context` parameter. Each mode determines which spatial information is incorporated during prediction.

### Context Mode Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input: Image Features"]
    
    subgraph spot["Mode: 'spot'"]
        S1["Single spot tile<br/>(55μm)"]
    end
    
    subgraph spot_subspot["Mode: 'spot_subspot'"]
        S2["Spot + 9 sub-tiles<br/>(3x3 grid, ~18μm each)"]
    end
    
    subgraph spot_neighbors["Mode: 'spot_neighbors'"]
        S3["Spot + neighboring spots<br/>(radius=1)"]
    end
    
    subgraph spot_subspot_neighbors["Mode: 'spot_subspot_neighbors'"]
        S4["Spot + sub-tiles +<br/>neighbors"]
    end
    
    Input --> spot
    Input --> spot_subspot
    Input --> spot_neighbors
    Input --> spot_subspot_neighbors
    
    S1 --> P1["_forward_spot<br/>phi_multiplier = 1"]
    S2 --> P2["_forward_spot_subspot<br/>phi_multiplier = 2"]
    S3 --> P3["_forward_spot_neighbors<br/>phi_multiplier = 2"]
    S4 --> P4["_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors<br/>phi_multiplier = 3"]
    
    P1 --> Output["Gene Expression Predictions"]
    P2 --> Output
    P3 --> Output
    P4 --> Output
```

### Mode Details

#### 1. `spot` - Basic Spot Context
- **Forward Method**: `_forward_spot` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:163-165]())
- **Phi Multiplier**: 1 (single feature vector)
- **Input**: Single spot-level feature vector
- **Use Case**: Simplest mode, suitable when sub-spot heterogeneity is not critical

#### 2. `spot_subspot` - Spot with Sub-tiles
- **Forward Method**: `_forward_spot_subspot` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:167-172]())
- **Phi Multiplier**: 2 (spot + aggregated sub-spots)
- **Input**: Spot feature + 9 mini-tile features (3×3 grid)
- **Use Case**: Captures sub-spot morphological heterogeneity within each 55μm spot

#### 3. `spot_neighbors` - Spot with Neighborhood
- **Forward Method**: `_forward_spot_neighbors` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:174-179]())
- **Phi Multiplier**: 2 (spot + aggregated neighbors)
- **Input**: Central spot feature + neighboring spot features
- **Use Case**: Incorporates spatial context from surrounding tissue

#### 4. `spot_subspot_neighbors` - Full Context (Default)
- **Forward Method**: `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:181-187]())
- **Phi Multiplier**: 3 (spot + sub-spots + neighbors)
- **Input**: Central spot + mini-tiles + neighbor spots
- **Use Case**: Most comprehensive mode, capturing both sub-spot detail and spatial context

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-187](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-117](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:119-126]()

---

## Forward Pass Architecture

### Data Flow Through Phi-Rho Ensemble

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input Features<br/>(varies by context mode)"]
    
    subgraph PhiStage["Phi Ensemble Stage"]
        PhiModules["n_ensemble_phi modules<br/>(default: 10)"]
        PhiMedian["Median Aggregation<br/>(across ensemble)"]
        PhiAgg["Context-Specific Aggregation<br/>(sum/mean/max for neighbors)"]
    end
    
    subgraph ConcatStage["Concatenation Stage"]
        Concat["Concatenate Phi Outputs<br/>(spot + subspot + neighbors)"]
    end
    
    subgraph RhoStage["Rho Ensemble Stage"]
        RhoModules["n_ensemble_rho modules<br/>(default: 10)"]
        RhoMean["Mean Aggregation<br/>(across ensemble)"]
    end
    
    Output["Gene Expression Predictions<br/>(output_size dimensions)"]
    
    Input --> PhiModules
    PhiModules --> PhiMedian
    PhiMedian --> PhiAgg
    PhiAgg --> Concat
    Concat --> RhoModules
    RhoModules --> RhoMean
    RhoMean --> Output
```

### Phi Application Logic

The `_apply_phi` method ([deepspot/spot/model.py:189-208]()) processes input features through the Phi ensemble:

1. **Reshape**: Flatten batch and sample dimensions to `(batch_size * sample_size, input_size)`
2. **Ensemble Processing**: Apply all Phi modules in parallel, producing `(n_ensemble, batch_size * sample_size, phi2rho_size)` tensor
3. **Median Aggregation**: Compute median across ensemble dimension for robustness
4. **Reshape Back**: Restore to `(batch_size, sample_size, phi2rho_size)`
5. **Context Aggregation**: Apply operation based on context:
   - `Operation.NONE`: Flatten to `(batch_size, sample_size * phi2rho_size)`
   - `Operation.SUM`: Sum across sample dimension
   - `Operation.MEAN`: Average across sample dimension
   - `Operation.MAX`: Max-pool across sample dimension

### Rho Application Logic

The `_apply_rho` method ([deepspot/spot/model.py:210-213]()) generates final predictions:

1. **Ensemble Processing**: Apply all Rho modules in parallel to concatenated Phi outputs
2. **Mean Aggregation**: Average predictions across ensemble for stability
3. **Output**: Return gene expression predictions of shape `(batch_size, output_size)`

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:189-213]()

---

## Context-Specific Forward Methods

### Forward Method Dispatch

```mermaid
graph LR
    Forward["forward(x)"]
    Dispatch["_forward_fn<br/>(set during __init__)"]
    
    Forward --> Dispatch
    
    Dispatch --> Spot["_forward_spot(x)"]
    Dispatch --> SubSpot["_forward_spot_subspot(x)"]
    Dispatch --> Neighbors["_forward_spot_neighbors(x)"]
    Dispatch --> Full["_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors(x)"]
    
    Spot --> PhiSpot["_apply_phi(x, phi_spot,<br/>operation=NONE)"]
    SubSpot --> PhiSpot2["_apply_phi(x_spot, phi_spot)<br/>+ _apply_phi(x_subspot, phi_subspot)"]
    Neighbors --> PhiSpot3["_apply_phi(x_spot, phi_spot)<br/>+ _apply_phi(x_neighbors, phi_neighbors,<br/>operation=agg_neighbors)"]
    Full --> PhiSpot4["All three Phi applications"]
    
    PhiSpot --> Rho1["_apply_rho(x_phi)"]
    PhiSpot2 --> Concat1["torch.cat((x_spot, x_subspot))"]
    PhiSpot3 --> Concat2["torch.cat((x_spot, x_neighbors))"]
    PhiSpot4 --> Concat3["torch.cat((x_spot, x_subspot, x_neighbors))"]
    
    Concat1 --> Rho2["_apply_rho(x_phi)"]
    Concat2 --> Rho3["_apply_rho(x_phi)"]
    Concat3 --> Rho4["_apply_rho(x_phi)"]
    
    Rho1 --> Output["Gene Predictions"]
    Rho2 --> Output
    Rho3 --> Output
    Rho4 --> Output
```

### Implementation Details

#### `_forward_spot` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:163-165]())
```python
# Input: x (single tensor)
# Phi multiplier: 1
x_phi = _apply_phi(x, phi_spot, operation=NONE)
return _apply_rho(x_phi)
```

#### `_forward_spot_subspot` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:167-172]())
```python
# Input: [x_spot, x_subspot] (list of 2 tensors)
# Phi multiplier: 2
x_spot_phi = _apply_phi(x_spot, phi_spot)
x_subspot_phi = _apply_phi(x_subspot, phi_subspot)
x_phi = torch.cat((x_spot_phi, x_subspot_phi), dim=1)
return _apply_rho(x_phi)
```

#### `_forward_spot_neighbors` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:174-179]())
```python
# Input: [x_spot, x_neighbors] (list of 2 tensors)
# Phi multiplier: 2
x_spot_phi = _apply_phi(x_spot, phi_spot)
x_neighbors_phi = _apply_phi(x_neighbors, phi_neighbors, operation=agg_neighbors)
x_phi = torch.cat((x_spot_phi, x_neighbors_phi), dim=1)
return _apply_rho(x_phi)
```

#### `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:181-187]())
```python
# Input: [x_spot, x_subspot, x_neighbors] (list of 3 tensors)
# Phi multiplier: 3
x_spot_phi = _apply_phi(x_spot, phi_spot)
x_subspot_phi = _apply_phi(x_subspot, phi_subspot)
x_neighbors_phi = _apply_phi(x_neighbors, phi_neighbors, operation=agg_neighbors)
x_phi = torch.cat((x_spot_phi, x_subspot_phi, x_neighbors_phi), dim=1)
return _apply_rho(x_phi)
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-187]()

---

## Training Lifecycle

### Training Loop Architecture

The `DeepSpot` model implements standard PyTorch Lightning training hooks with custom loss tracking.

```mermaid
graph TB
    TrainData["Training DataLoader"]
    ValData["Validation DataLoader"]
    
    TrainData --> TrainStep["training_step(batch, batch_idx)"]
    ValData --> ValStep["validation_step(batch, batch_idx)"]
    
    TrainStep --> LoopStep1["loop_step(batch, 'train')"]
    ValStep --> LoopStep2["loop_step(batch, 'val')"]
    
    subgraph LoopStep["loop_step Logic"]
        Unpack["Unpack batch: X, y"]
        Cast["Cast to float: X.float(), y.float()"]
        Forward["y_hat = forward(X)"]
        Loss["loss = loss_func(y_hat, y)"]
        Log["self.log(stage, loss)"]
        Track["Append to training_loss or<br/>validation_loss"]
    end
    
    LoopStep1 --> Unpack
    LoopStep2 --> Unpack
    Unpack --> Cast
    Cast --> Forward
    Forward --> Loss
    Loss --> Log
    Log --> Track
    Track --> Return["Return loss"]
    
    Return --> Optimizer["AdamW Optimizer<br/>(configured in configure_optimizers)"]
    Optimizer --> Update["Update model parameters"]
```

### Method Implementations

#### `training_step` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:148-149]())
Delegates to `loop_step` with stage `"train"`.

#### `validation_step` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:151-152]())
Delegates to `loop_step` with stage `"val"`.

#### `loop_step` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:128-146]())
Core training logic:
1. Unpack batch into features `X` and targets `y`
2. Cast to float tensors (handle list or single tensor for `X`)
3. Forward pass: `y_hat = self(X)`
4. Compute loss using configured loss function
5. Log loss to Lightning for monitoring
6. Append to internal loss tracking (`training_loss` or `validation_loss` lists)
7. Return loss for backpropagation

#### `configure_optimizers` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:215-217]() equivalent to DeepCell [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218]())
Returns AdamW optimizer with specified learning rate and weight decay.

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:128-152](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:144-168](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218]()

---

## Loss Function Configuration

The model supports multiple loss functions specified during initialization. The mapping from string identifiers to loss function implementations is performed in `__init__`:

| `loss_func` String | Loss Function | Module Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `"mse"` | Mean Squared Error | `loss_mse_function` [deepspot/spot/loss.py:19-21]() |
| `"cos"` | Cosine Similarity Loss | `loss_cosine_function` |
| `"l1"` | L1 (Mean Absolute Error) | `loss_l1_function` |
| `"huber"` | Huber Loss | `loss_huber_function` |
| `"mse_cos"` | MSE + Cosine (combined) | `loss_mse_cosine_function` |
| `"l1_cos"` | L1 + Cosine (combined) | `loss_l1_cosine_function` |
| `"huber_cos"` | Huber + Cosine (combined) | `loss_huber_cosine_function` |
| `"pearson"` | Pearson Correlation Loss | `loss_pearson_function` |
| `"mse_pearson"` | MSE + Pearson (combined) | `loss_mse_pearson_function` |
| `"poisson"` | Poisson Loss | `loss_poisson_function` |

For detailed information on each loss function's implementation, see [Loss Functions](#5.4).

**Sources**: [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:93-99]()

---

## Utility Methods

### `inverse_transform` 
Similar to DeepCell implementation ([deepspot/cell/model.py:174-177]()), applies inverse scaling transformation if a scaler was provided during initialization.

### `plot_loss`
Similar to DeepCell implementation ([deepspot/cell/model.py:235-281]()), visualizes training and validation loss curves with exponential smoothing for trend analysis.

### `_get_phi_multiplier` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:110-117]())
Determines the concatenated feature dimension based on context mode:

| Context Mode | Phi Multiplier | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| `"spot"` | 1 | Only spot features |
| `"spot_subspot"` | 2 | Spot + subspot features |
| `"spot_neighbors"` | 2 | Spot + neighbor features |
| `"spot_subspot_neighbors"` | 3 | Spot + subspot + neighbor features |

### `_get_forward_function` ([deepspot/spot/model.py:119-126]())
Returns the appropriate forward method based on `spot_context` string during initialization. This enables runtime dispatch without if-else branching in the `forward` method.

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-126](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:174-177](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:235-281]()

## Model Instantiation Example

### Basic Configuration

```python
from deepspot.spot.model import DeepSpot

# Initialize model for 500 genes with UNI features (1024-dim)
model = DeepSpot(
    input_size=1024,           # UNI embedding dimension
    output_size=500,           # Number of genes to predict
    loss_func="mse_pearson",   # Combined MSE + Pearson loss
    lr=1e-4,                   # Learning rate
    p=0.2,                     # Dropout probability
    n_ensemble=10,             # Ensemble size
    phi2rho_size=1024,         # Intermediate dimension
    spot_context="spot_subspot_neighbors",  # Full context mode
    agg_neighbors="max",       # Max-pooling for neighbors
    random_seed=2024
)
```

### Advanced Configuration with Custom Ensemble Sizes

```python
model = DeepSpot(
    input_size=1536,           # Hoptimus0 embedding dimension
    output_size=800,           # 800 highly variable genes
    loss_func="huber_cos",     # Huber + Cosine loss
    lr=5e-5,                   # Lower learning rate
    p_phi=0.3,                 # Higher dropout for Phi
    p_rho=0.1,                 # Lower dropout for Rho
    n_ensemble_phi=15,         # Larger Phi ensemble
    n_ensemble_rho=8,          # Smaller Rho ensemble
    phi2rho_size=2048,         # Larger intermediate dimension
    weight_decay=1e-5,         # Stronger L2 regularization
    spot_context="spot_neighbors",  # Use neighbors only
    agg_neighbors="mean",      # Mean aggregation
    scaler=StandardScaler()    # Provide scaler for inverse transform
)
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:59-108]()

## Code-to-Concept Mapping

### Class Architecture Overview

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DeepSpot {
        +int input_size
        +int output_size
        +str loss_func
        +float lr
        +ModuleList phi_spot
        +ModuleList phi_subspot
        +ModuleList phi_neighbors
        +ModuleList rho
        +Operation agg_neighbors
        +List training_loss
        +List validation_loss
        +__init__(...)
        +forward(x)
        +training_step(batch, batch_idx)
        +validation_step(batch, batch_idx)
        +loop_step(batch, stage)
        +_forward_spot(x)
        +_forward_spot_subspot(x)
        +_forward_spot_neighbors(x)
        +_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors(x)
        +_apply_phi(x, phi_modules, operation)
        +_apply_rho(x_phi)
        +configure_optimizers()
        +inverse_transform(x)
        +plot_loss()
    }
    
    class Phi {
        +Sequential model
        +__init__(input_size, output_size, p)
        +forward(x)
    }
    
    class Rho {
        +Sequential model
        +__init__(input_size, output_size, p)
        +forward(x)
    }
    
    class LightningModule {
        <<PyTorch Lightning>>
    }
    
    class Operation {
        <<Enum>>
        SUM
        MAX
        MEAN
        NONE
    }
    
    DeepSpot --|> LightningModule
    DeepSpot --> Phi : contains n_ensemble_phi instances
    DeepSpot --> Rho : contains n_ensemble_rho instances
    DeepSpot --> Operation : uses for aggregation
```

### Relationship to Data Loaders

```mermaid
graph LR
    DSLoader["DeepSpotDataLoader"]
    Model["DeepSpot Model"]
    
    subgraph DataOutput["DataLoader Output Shapes"]
        Context1["spot: (batch, 1, input_size)"]
        Context2["spot_subspot:<br/>(batch, 1, input_size)<br/>(batch, 9, input_size)"]
        Context3["spot_neighbors:<br/>(batch, 1, input_size)<br/>(batch, n_neighbors, input_size)"]
        Context4["spot_subspot_neighbors:<br/>(batch, 1, input_size)<br/>(batch, 9, input_size)<br/>(batch, n_neighbors, input_size)"]
    end
    
    DSLoader --> Context1
    DSLoader --> Context2
    DSLoader --> Context3
    DSLoader --> Context4
    
    Context1 --> Model
    Context2 --> Model
    Context3 --> Model
    Context4 --> Model
    
    Model --> Predictions["Gene Expression Predictions<br/>(batch, output_size)"]
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/spot/model.py:58-217](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-60]()

---

# Page: Phi and Rho Neural Layers

# Phi and Rho Neural Layers

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.codeboarding/Core Utilities.md](.codeboarding/Core Utilities.md)
- [deepspot/cell/model.py](deepspot/cell/model.py)

</details>



This document explains the `Phi` and `Rho` neural network modules, which form the core computational building blocks of both DeepSpot and DeepCell models. These modules implement a two-stage ensemble architecture for transforming input features (Phi) and generating final predictions (Rho). For information about how these layers are integrated into complete model architectures, see [DeepCell Model](#5.1) and [DeepSpot Model](#5.2). For the loss functions used to train these modules, see [Loss Functions](#5.4).

## Overview

The Phi-Rho architecture implements a permutation-invariant deep-set approach where:
- **Phi modules** transform input features from foundation models into an intermediate representation
- **Rho modules** map the intermediate representation to gene expression predictions
- Both stages use **ensemble learning** with multiple parallel networks and aggregation strategies

This design enables the models to process variable-sized inputs (e.g., multiple sub-tiles or neighbor cells) while maintaining robust predictions through ensemble averaging.

## Phi Neural Layer

### Architecture

The `Phi` class implements a simple three-layer neural network that transforms input features into an intermediate representation.

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Input Features<br/>(foundation model embeddings)"]
    Linear["Linear Layer<br/>input_size → output_size"]
    Dropout["Dropout Layer<br/>(rate = p_phi)"]
    ReLU["ReLU Activation<br/>(inplace=True)"]
    Output["Transformed Features<br/>(phi2rho_size dims)"]
    
    Input --> Linear
    Linear --> Dropout
    Dropout --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Output
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-46](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:31-41]()

### Implementation Details

| Component | Configuration | Purpose |
|-----------|--------------|---------|
| Input Layer | `nn.Linear(input_size, output_size)` | Projects features to intermediate dimension |
| Dropout | `nn.Dropout(p=p_phi)` | Regularization to prevent overfitting |
| Activation | `nn.ReLU(inplace=True)` | Non-linear transformation |
| Output Size | `phi2rho_size` (default: 1024) | Intermediate representation dimension |

The `Phi` module receives foundation model embeddings with varying dimensions:
- UNI: 1024-dimensional features
- Hoptimus0: 1536-dimensional features  
- Phikon: 768-dimensional features
- Inception: 2048-dimensional features

All are projected to a common `phi2rho_size` dimension for consistency.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-46](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:31-41]()

### Role in Forward Pass

The `Phi` module serves as a feature normalizer and transformer, enabling different foundation models to work with a common downstream architecture. Multiple Phi modules are instantiated in an ensemble, and their outputs are aggregated using median pooling (see Ensemble Architecture section).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-209]()

## Rho Neural Layer

### Architecture

The `Rho` class implements the final prediction stage, mapping intermediate representations to gene expression values.

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Phi Output<br/>(concatenated contexts)"]
    Dropout1["Dropout Layer<br/>(rate = p_rho)"]
    ReLU["ReLU Activation<br/>(inplace=True)"]
    Linear["Linear Layer<br/>input_size → output_size"]
    Dropout2["Dropout Layer<br/>(rate = 0.1)"]
    Output["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    
    Input --> Dropout1
    Dropout1 --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Linear
    Linear --> Dropout2
    Dropout2 --> Output
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:49-60](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:44-55]()

### Implementation Details

| Component | Configuration | Purpose |
|-----------|--------------|---------|
| Input Dropout | `nn.Dropout(p=p_rho)` | Regularization on Phi outputs |
| Activation | `nn.ReLU(inplace=True)` | Non-linear transformation |
| Output Layer | `nn.Linear(input_size, output_size)` | Maps to gene expression space |
| Final Dropout | `nn.Dropout(p=0.1)` | Fixed regularization on predictions |

The `Rho` module's input size varies based on context mode:
- **Cell-only**: `phi2rho_size` (e.g., 1024)
- **Cell + neighbors**: `2 * phi2rho_size` (e.g., 2048)
- **Spot-only**: `phi2rho_size`
- **Spot + subspot**: `2 * phi2rho_size`
- **Spot + neighbors**: `2 * phi2rho_size`
- **Spot + subspot + neighbors**: `3 * phi2rho_size` (e.g., 3072)

The output size equals the number of genes being predicted (typically 300-800 for spots, 500 for cells).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:49-60](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:126-127](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:44-55]()

## Ensemble Architecture

### Ensemble Configuration

Both Phi and Rho stages use ensemble learning with multiple parallel networks to improve prediction robustness.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Phi Ensemble (n_ensemble_phi = 10)"
        Phi1["Phi Module 1"]
        Phi2["Phi Module 2"]
        PhiDots["..."]
        Phi10["Phi Module 10"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Aggregation"
        MedianAgg["Median Aggregation<br/>torch.median(dim=1)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rho Ensemble (n_ensemble_rho = 10)"
        Rho1["Rho Module 1"]
        Rho2["Rho Module 2"]
        RhoDots["..."]
        Rho10["Rho Module 10"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Final Aggregation"
        MeanAgg["Mean Aggregation<br/>torch.mean(dim=1)"]
    end
    
    Input["Input Features"] --> Phi1
    Input --> Phi2
    Input --> PhiDots
    Input --> Phi10
    
    Phi1 --> MedianAgg
    Phi2 --> MedianAgg
    PhiDots --> MedianAgg
    Phi10 --> MedianAgg
    
    MedianAgg --> Rho1
    MedianAgg --> Rho2
    MedianAgg --> RhoDots
    MedianAgg --> Rho10
    
    Rho1 --> MeanAgg
    Rho2 --> MeanAgg
    RhoDots --> MeanAgg
    Rho10 --> MeanAgg
    
    MeanAgg --> Output["Gene Expression Predictions"]
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:125-127](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-214]()

### Phi Ensemble Aggregation

The `_apply_phi` method processes inputs through all Phi modules and aggregates using **median** pooling:

```python
# From _apply_phi implementation
x_phi = torch.stack([phi(x) for phi in phi_modules], dim=1)
x_phi, _ = torch.median(x_phi, dim=1)  # Median ensemble aggregation
```

**Key steps:**
1. Apply all `n_ensemble_phi` modules in parallel (default: 10)
2. Stack outputs along dimension 1
3. Compute element-wise median across ensemble members
4. Apply spatial aggregation operation (SUM, MEAN, MAX, or NONE) based on context

**Aggregation operations:**
- `Operation.NONE`: Keep all samples (for single cell/spot)
- `Operation.MAX`: Take maximum across samples (default for neighbors)
- `Operation.MEAN`: Average across samples
- `Operation.SUM`: Sum across samples

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-209](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:189-208]()

### Rho Ensemble Aggregation

The `_apply_rho` method processes Phi outputs through all Rho modules and aggregates using **mean** pooling:

```python
# From _apply_rho implementation
x_rho = torch.stack([rho(x_phi) for rho in self.rho], dim=1)
x_rho = torch.mean(x_rho, dim=1)  # Mean ensemble aggregation
```

**Key steps:**
1. Apply all `n_ensemble_rho` modules in parallel (default: 10)
2. Stack outputs along dimension 1
3. Compute element-wise mean across ensemble members

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:211-214](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:210-213]()

### Rationale for Different Aggregation Strategies

The architecture uses **median aggregation for Phi** and **mean aggregation for Rho**:
- **Median (Phi):** Robust to outliers in feature transformations, ensuring stable intermediate representations
- **Mean (Rho):** Provides smooth averaging of final predictions across ensemble members

## Integration in Forward Pass

### Data Flow Through Phi-Rho Layers

The following diagram shows how inputs flow through Phi and Rho modules in different context modes:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Cell Context: cell_neighbors"
        CellInput["x_cell<br/>(batch, 1, input_size)"]
        NeighInput["x_neighbors<br/>(batch, n_neighbors, input_size)"]
        
        CellPhi["_apply_phi(x_cell)<br/>operation=NONE"]
        NeighPhi["_apply_phi(x_neighbors)<br/>operation=agg_neighbors"]
        
        Concat["torch.cat(dim=1)"]
        ApplyRho["_apply_rho"]
        
        CellInput --> CellPhi
        NeighInput --> NeighPhi
        CellPhi --> Concat
        NeighPhi --> Concat
        Concat --> ApplyRho
        ApplyRho --> CellOutput["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Spot Context: spot_subspot_neighbors"
        SpotInput["x_spot<br/>(batch, 1, input_size)"]
        SubspotInput["x_subspot<br/>(batch, 9, input_size)"]
        NeighborsInput["x_neighbors<br/>(batch, n_neighbors, input_size)"]
        
        SpotPhi["_apply_phi(x_spot)<br/>operation=NONE"]
        SubspotPhi["_apply_phi(x_subspot)<br/>operation=MAX"]
        NeighborsPhi["_apply_phi(x_neighbors)<br/>operation=agg_neighbors"]
        
        Concat2["torch.cat(dim=1)"]
        ApplyRho2["_apply_rho"]
        
        SpotInput --> SpotPhi
        SubspotInput --> SubspotPhi
        NeighborsInput --> NeighborsPhi
        SpotPhi --> Concat2
        SubspotPhi --> Concat2
        NeighborsPhi --> Concat2
        Concat2 --> ApplyRho2
        ApplyRho2 --> SpotOutput["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    end
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:183-188](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:181-187]()

### Context-Specific Forward Methods

Both DeepCell and DeepSpot implement multiple forward methods that leverage Phi-Rho layers differently:

**DeepCell forward methods:**
- `_forward_cell`: Single cell only → `_apply_phi` (NONE) → `_apply_rho`
- `_forward_cell_neighbors`: Cell + neighbors → two `_apply_phi` calls → concatenate → `_apply_rho`

**DeepSpot forward methods:**
- `_forward_spot`: Single spot → `_apply_phi` (NONE) → `_apply_rho`
- `_forward_spot_subspot`: Spot + 9 sub-tiles → two `_apply_phi` calls → concatenate → `_apply_rho`
- `_forward_spot_neighbors`: Spot + neighbors → two `_apply_phi` calls → concatenate → `_apply_rho`
- `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors`: Full context → three `_apply_phi` calls → concatenate → `_apply_rho`

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:179-188](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-187]()

## Hyperparameter Configuration

### Initialization Parameters

The following table summarizes key hyperparameters for Phi and Rho modules:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `input_size` | Varies | Foundation model embedding dimension |
| `output_size` | Varies | Number of genes to predict |
| `phi2rho_size` | 1024 | Intermediate dimension between Phi and Rho |
| `p` | 0.2 | Base dropout probability |
| `p_phi` | `p` | Dropout rate for Phi modules |
| `p_rho` | `p` | Dropout rate for Rho modules |
| `n_ensemble` | 10 | Base number of ensemble members |
| `n_ensemble_phi` | `n_ensemble` | Number of Phi modules in ensemble |
| `n_ensemble_rho` | `n_ensemble` | Number of Rho modules in ensemble |

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:64-82](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:59-77]()

### Module Instantiation

During model initialization, Phi and Rho ensembles are created as `nn.ModuleList` objects:

```python
# Phi ensemble for cell/spot features
self.phi_cell = nn.ModuleList([
    Phi(input_size, phi2rho_size, self.p_phi) 
    for _ in range(self.n_ensemble_phi)
])

# Rho ensemble for final predictions
self.rho = nn.ModuleList([
    Rho(phi2rho_size * multiplier, output_size, self.p_rho) 
    for _ in range(self.n_ensemble_rho)
])
```

The `multiplier` value depends on the context mode (1 for single cell/spot, 2 for cell+neighbors, 3 for spot+subspot+neighbors).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:125-127](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:120-122]()

### Dropout Strategy

The architecture employs **three dropout layers** per forward pass:
1. **Phi module:** Applied after the linear layer (rate = `p_phi`)
2. **Rho module (input):** Applied before the final linear layer (rate = `p_rho`)
3. **Rho module (output):** Fixed dropout at 0.1 applied to predictions

This aggressive regularization strategy prevents overfitting when training on limited spatial transcriptomics samples.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-60]()

## Code Mapping Reference

The following table maps conceptual components to their code implementations:

| Concept | DeepCell Implementation | DeepSpot Implementation |
|---------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Phi class | [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-46]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:31-41]() |
| Rho class | [deepspot/cell/model.py:49-60]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:44-55]() |
| Phi ensemble creation | [deepspot/cell/model.py:125]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:120]() |
| Rho ensemble creation | [deepspot/cell/model.py:126-127]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:121-122]() |
| `_apply_phi` method | [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-209]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:189-208]() |
| `_apply_rho` method | [deepspot/cell/model.py:211-214]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:210-213]() |
| Aggregation operations | [deepspot/cell/model.py:29-33]() | [deepspot/spot/model.py:24-28]() |

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:1-277]()
