# Page: Workflows

# Workflows

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb](example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb)
- [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb](example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb)
- [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb](example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb)

</details>



This page provides an overview of the complete end-to-end workflows for predicting spatial transcriptomics from H&E images using DeepSpot. It covers the two main resolution-specific pipelines: **Visium spot-level** workflow ([section 7.1](#7.1)) and **Xenium cell-level** workflow ([section 7.2](#7.2)). Each workflow consists of three sequential stages: preprocessing, training, and inference.

For installation and environment setup, see [Installation](#2.1). For architectural details about the models themselves, see [Model Architecture](#5). For detailed API documentation of the classes and functions used in these workflows, see [API Reference](#9).

---

## Workflow Architecture

Both workflows follow a three-stage pipeline pattern, but operate at different spatial resolutions and use resolution-specific data loaders and models.

### Complete Workflow Stages

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Stage 1: Preprocessing"
        Input["Raw Data<br/>• H&E Images (.svs, .tiff, .jpg)<br/>• AnnData (.h5ad)"]
        GeneSelect["Gene Selection<br/>scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes()"]
        FeatureExtract["Feature Extraction<br/>get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()<br/>crop_tile()"]
        SpatialProcess["Spatial Processing<br/>neighbor computation<br/>coordinate storage"]
        
        Input --> GeneSelect
        Input --> FeatureExtract
        FeatureExtract --> SpatialProcess
        
        Output1["Preprocessed Data<br/>• .npy embeddings per spot/cell<br/>• .pkl gene counts<br/>• .csv gene metadata"]
        GeneSelect --> Output1
        SpatialProcess --> Output1
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Training"
        Loader["Data Loading<br/>DeepSpotDataLoader /<br/>DeepCellDataLoader"]
        Model["Model Training<br/>DeepSpot / DeepCell"]
        Trainer["Lightning Trainer<br/>EarlyStopping callbacks"]
        
        Output1 --> Loader
        Loader --> Model
        Model --> Trainer
        
        Output2["Trained Model<br/>• .pkl weights<br/>• .yaml hyperparameters<br/>• scaler object"]
        Trainer --> Output2
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Inference"
        NewImage["New H&E Image"]
        Coords["Spot/Cell<br/>Coordinates"]
        InferFunc["Prediction Function<br/>predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()<br/>predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()"]
        
        NewImage --> InferFunc
        Coords --> InferFunc
        Output2 --> InferFunc
        
        Output3["Predictions<br/>AnnData with predicted<br/>gene expression"]
        InferFunc --> Output3
    end
    
    style Input fill:#f9f9f9
    style Output1 fill:#f9f9f9
    style Output2 fill:#f9f9f9
    style Output3 fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [README.md:60-73](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb:1-359](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb:1-363](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:1-374]()

## Spot vs Cell Workflow Comparison

The system provides two parallel workflows optimized for different spatial transcriptomics technologies:

| Aspect | Visium Spot Workflow ([7.1](#7.1)) | Xenium Cell Workflow ([7.2](#7.2)) |
|--------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Resolution** | ~55μm spot diameter | ~20μm cell diameter |
| **Technology** | Visium spot-level | Xenium single-cell |
| **Data Loader** | `DeepSpotDataLoader` | `DeepCellDataLoader` |
| **Model** | `DeepSpot` | `DeepCell` |
| **Gene Count** | 300-800 highly variable genes | ~500 highly variable genes |
| **Spatial Context** | 4 modes: spot, subspot, neighbors, full | 2 modes: cell, cell_neighbors |
| **Mini-tiling** | 3×3 sub-tiles per spot | Not used (cells are small) |
| **Neighbor Context** | `radius=1` (default) | `n_neighbors=45` (typical) |
| **Preprocessing Notebooks** | `GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_1_preprocessing.ipynb` | `GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb` |
| **Training Notebooks** | `GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_2_training.ipynb` | `GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training.ipynb` |
| **Inference Notebooks** | `GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3_inference.ipynb` | `GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference.ipynb` |

**Sources:** [README.md:64-73]()

---

## Preprocessing Stage Details

The preprocessing stage transforms raw spatial transcriptomics data and H&E images into a format suitable for model training.

### Key Preprocessing Steps

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Input: AnnData + H&E Image"]
    
    Step1["Load Data<br/>scanpy.read_h5ad()"]
    Step2["Select HVGs<br/>scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes()<br/>n_top_genes=300-800 (spot)<br/>n_top_genes=500 (cell)"]
    Step3["Save Gene Metadata<br/>adata.var.to_csv()"]
    Step4["Save Count Matrix<br/>pandas.to_pickle()"]
    
    Step5["Load Foundation Model<br/>get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()"]
    Step6["Load Image<br/>pyvips.Image.new_from_file()"]
    Step7["Extract Tile Features<br/>Loop: crop_tile() + model()"]
    Step8["Save Embeddings<br/>np.save() per spot/cell"]
    
    Start --> Step1
    Step1 --> Step2
    Step2 --> Step3
    Step2 --> Step4
    
    Start --> Step5
    Start --> Step6
    Step6 --> Step7
    Step5 --> Step7
    Step7 --> Step8
    
    Step3 --> Output["Preprocessed Data Ready"]
    Step4 --> Output
    Step8 --> Output
```

### File Organization After Preprocessing

The preprocessing stage creates the following directory structure:

```
out_folder/
├── data/
│   ├── inputX/
│   │   └── {sample_id}.pkl          # Gene count matrices
│   ├── image_features/
│   │   └── {model_name}_{diameter}/
│   │       └── {sample_id}/
│   │           ├── {barcode_1}.npy  # Per-spot/cell embeddings
│   │           ├── {barcode_2}.npy
│   │           └── ...
│   └── info_highly_variable_genes_{technology}.csv  # Gene metadata
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb:109-114](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb:189-206](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_1_preprocessing.ipynb:242-308]()

---

## Training Stage Details

The training stage uses data loaders to batch preprocessed features and trains the neural network models.

### Training Configuration Parameters

| Parameter Category | Spot Workflow | Cell Workflow |
|-------------------|---------------|---------------|
| **Data Loader Class** | `DeepSpotDataLoader` | `DeepCellDataLoader` |
| **Model Class** | `DeepSpot` | `DeepCell` |
| **Context Mode** | `spot_context` (4 options) | `cell_context` (2 options) |
| **Batch Size** | Configurable (e.g., 1024) | Configurable (e.g., 1024) |
| **Normalization** | `'standard'` / `None` | `'standard'` / `None` |
| **Spatial Resolution** | `resolution` parameter | `resolution` parameter |
| **Optimizer** | AdamW (default) | AdamW (default) |
| **Loss Function** | MSE + Pearson (default) | MSE + Pearson (default) |

### Training Loop Components

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant NB as "Training Notebook"
    participant DL as "DeepSpotDataLoader /<br/>DeepCellDataLoader"
    participant TL as "torch.utils.data.DataLoader"
    participant M as "DeepSpot / DeepCell"
    participant T as "lightning.Trainer"
    participant ES as "EarlyStopping"
    
    NB->>DL: Initialize with out_folder,<br/>samples, genes_to_keep
    DL->>DL: Load preprocessed data<br/>compute neighbors
    NB->>TL: Wrap with batch_size,<br/>num_workers
    NB->>M: Initialize model with<br/>input_size, output_size, scaler
    NB->>T: Create trainer with<br/>max_epochs, callbacks
    T->>TL: Request batch
    TL->>DL: __getitem__()
    DL->>TL: Return X, y
    TL->>T: Batched data
    T->>M: training_step(X, y)
    M->>M: forward() + loss()
    M->>T: loss value
    T->>ES: Check stopping criteria
    ES-->>T: Continue / Stop
    T->>NB: Training complete
    NB->>NB: torch.save(model)
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb:86-117](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb:162-177](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb:230-240]()

---

## Inference Stage Details

The inference stage applies trained models to new H&E images to predict spatial gene expression.

### Inference Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Preparation"
        I1["New H&E Image Path"]
        I2["Spot/Cell Coordinates<br/>from AnnData.obs"]
        I3["Model Weights (.pkl)"]
        I4["Model Hyperparameters (.yaml)"]
        I5["Gene List (.csv)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inference Execution"
        P1["Load Model<br/>torch.load()"]
        P2["model.eval()<br/>model.to(device)"]
        P3["Load Foundation Model<br/>get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()"]
        P4["predict_*_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()"]
        P5["On-the-fly Feature Extraction<br/>crop_tile() + morphology_model()"]
        P6["Model Forward Pass<br/>with neighbor context"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-processing"
        O1["Rescale Predictions<br/>model.inverse_transform()"]
        O2["Clip Negative Values<br/>counts[counts < 0] = 0"]
        O3["Create AnnData<br/>with predictions"]
        O4["Visualization<br/>squidpy.pl.spatial_scatter()"]
    end
    
    I1 --> P4
    I2 --> P4
    I3 --> P1
    I4 --> P1
    I5 --> O3
    
    P1 --> P2
    P2 --> P4
    P3 --> P4
    P4 --> P5
    P5 --> P6
    
    P6 --> O1
    O1 --> O2
    O2 --> O3
    O3 --> O4
```

### Key Inference Functions

| Function | Location | Purpose |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()` | `utils/utils_image.py` | Predict spot-level gene expression from image path |
| `predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()` | `utils/utils_image.py` | Predict cell-level gene expression from image path |
| `crop_tile()` | `utils/utils_image.py` | Extract image tiles at specified coordinates |
| `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()` | `utils/utils_image.py` | Load foundation model and preprocessing function |
| `model.inverse_transform()` | Model classes | Rescale normalized predictions to original ranges |

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:39-42](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:82-96](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:232-266](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:286-293]()

---

## Critical Post-Processing Step

**IMPORTANT:** Both workflows require manual rescaling of predictions using the model's `scaler` object:

```python
# Predictions are normalized during inference
expression_norm = model(X)  # Returns normalized values

# Must manually rescale to original ranges
expression = model.inverse_transform(expression_norm)

# Optional: clip negative predictions
expression[expression < 0] = 0
```

The `scaler` object used during training must be saved with model weights and loaded during inference. It is stored in the model checkpoint and accessible via `model.inverse_transform()`.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_2_training_xenium.ipynb:184-192](), [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:273-293]()

---

## Getting Started with Workflows

### Visium Spot Workflow ([7.1](#7.1))

For complete spot-level spatial transcriptomics prediction:

1. **Preprocessing ([7.1.1](#7.1.1))**: Extract spot features from H&E images, select highly variable genes (300-800), compute 3×3 mini-tiles per spot
2. **Training ([7.1.2](#7.1.2))**: Configure `DeepSpotDataLoader` with spatial context options, train `DeepSpot` model with chosen context mode
3. **Inference ([7.1.3](#7.1.3))**: Apply trained model to new images using `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()`

### Xenium Cell Workflow ([7.2](#7.2))

For complete cell-level spatial transcriptomics prediction:

1. **Preprocessing ([7.2.1](#7.2.1))**: Extract cell features from H&E images, select highly variable genes (~500), compute cell neighbors
2. **Training ([7.2.2](#7.2.2))**: Configure `DeepCellDataLoader` with `n_neighbors=45`, train `DeepCell` model
3. **Inference ([7.2.3](#7.2.3))**: Apply trained model to new images using `predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()`

### Notebook Locations

All example notebooks are located in the `example_notebook/` directory:

- Visium workflows: `example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/`
- Xenium workflows: `example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/`

**Sources:** [README.md:60-73]()

---

## Workflow Execution Time Considerations

| Stage | Visium Spot | Xenium Cell | Notes |
|-------|-------------|-------------|-------|
| **Preprocessing** | Hours | Hours | Depends on image size and number of spots/cells |
| **Training** | Minutes to hours | Minutes to hours | Depends on dataset size, epochs, and GPU |
| **Inference** | Minutes | Minutes | With precomputed embeddings: faster. On-the-fly: slower per image |

Preprocessing is the most time-consuming stage but only needs to be done once per dataset. Training can be repeated with different hyperparameters using the same preprocessed data. Inference with precomputed embeddings is significantly faster than on-the-fly feature extraction.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Xenium_single-cell_example/GettingStartedWithDeepCell_3_inference_xenium.ipynb:219-223]()

# Page: Visium Spot Workflow

# Visium Spot Workflow

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document provides a complete overview of the Visium spot-level spatial transcriptomics workflow, from raw H&E images and spatial transcriptomics data to trained models and predictions. The workflow operates at approximately 55μm spot resolution, where each spot captures expression from 1-10 cells. This page covers the end-to-end pipeline; for detailed steps, see [Visium Preprocessing](#7.1.1), [Visium Training](#7.1.2), and [Visium Inference](#7.1.3). For single-cell resolution workflows, see [Xenium Cell Workflow](#7.2).

**Sources:** [README.md:60-68]()

---

## Workflow Overview

The Visium spot workflow consists of three sequential stages that transform H&E histology images into predicted spatial transcriptomics data:

1. **Preprocessing**: Extract morphological features from H&E images, select highly variable genes, compute spatial relationships, and prepare data for training
2. **Training**: Train the `DeepSpot` model to learn mappings from image features to gene expression using `DeepSpotDataLoader`
3. **Inference**: Apply trained models to new H&E images to predict spatial transcriptomics, with optional use of pretrained weights from Zenodo

The workflow leverages pathology foundation models (UNI, Hoptimus0, Phikon) for feature extraction and supports multiple spatial context modes (individual spots, sub-spots, neighbors, or combinations).

**Sources:** [README.md:60-78]()

---

## Complete Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Stage 1: Preprocessing"
        HE["H&E Image<br/>.svs, .tiff, .jpg"]
        ST["Spatial Transcriptomics<br/>AnnData .h5ad"]
        
        GeneSelect["Gene Selection<br/>300-800 HVGs"]
        FeatureExtract["Feature Extraction<br/>crop_tile()<br/>get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()<br/>→ embeddings.npy"]
        SpatialComp["Spatial Computation<br/>Grid coordinates<br/>Mini-tiles (3x3)<br/>Neighbor graph"]
        
        HE --> FeatureExtract
        ST --> GeneSelect
        ST --> SpatialComp
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Training"
        DataLoader["DeepSpotDataLoader<br/>load_data()<br/>spatial upsampling<br/>smoothing<br/>normalization"]
        Model["DeepSpot<br/>Phi-Rho ensemble<br/>4 context modes"]
        Loss["Loss Functions<br/>MSE, Pearson"]
        Optimizer["AdamW Optimizer"]
        Weights["Trained Weights<br/>.pkl"]
        Config["Configuration<br/>.yaml"]
        
        GeneSelect --> DataLoader
        FeatureExtract --> DataLoader
        SpatialComp --> DataLoader
        DataLoader --> Model
        Model --> Loss
        Loss --> Optimizer
        Optimizer --> Model
        Model --> Weights
        Model --> Config
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Inference"
        NewImage["New H&E Image"]
        Coords["Spot Coordinates<br/>Grid generation"]
        PretrainedWeights["Pretrained Weights<br/>Zenodo or custom"]
        InferFunc["predict_spot_spatial_<br/>transcriptomics_from_image_path()"]
        Predictions["AnnData with<br/>predicted expression"]
        Viz["Visualization<br/>squidpy.pl.spatial_scatter()"]
        
        NewImage --> InferFunc
        Coords --> InferFunc
        PretrainedWeights --> InferFunc
        Weights -.-> InferFunc
        Config -.-> InferFunc
        InferFunc --> Predictions
        Predictions --> Viz
    end
    
    style HE fill:#f9f9f9
    style ST fill:#f9f9f9
    style DataLoader fill:#e8f4f8
    style Model fill:#e8f4f8
    style InferFunc fill:#e8f4f8
```

**Diagram: Complete Visium Spot Workflow showing three stages and key code entities**

**Sources:** [README.md:60-68](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:74-93]()

---

## Key Components and Code Entities

### Data Structures

| Component | Type | Description | Location |
|-----------|------|-------------|----------|
| Input AnnData | `anndata.AnnData` | Spatial transcriptomics with `.X` (counts), `.var` (genes), `.obs` (spot metadata), `.obsm['spatial']` (coordinates) | Preprocessing input |
| Feature Files | `.npy` arrays | Pre-extracted morphological features per spot, shape: `(n_features,)` | Preprocessing output |
| Training Config | `.yaml` | Hyperparameters: `spot_diameter`, `spot_distance`, `image_feature_model`, learning rate, batch size | Training configuration |
| Model Weights | `.pkl` | Serialized `DeepSpot` model with `Phi` and `Rho` ensembles | Training output |
| Gene Manifest | `.csv` | DataFrame with `gene_name`, `highly_variable_rank`, `isPredicted` columns | Training metadata |
| Prediction AnnData | `anndata.AnnData` | Output with predicted expression in `.X` | Inference output |

### Core Classes and Functions

| Entity | Type | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `DeepSpot` | Class | Spot-level prediction model with four context modes: `_forward_spot()`, `_forward_spot_subspot()`, `_forward_spot_neighbors()`, `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors()` |
| `DeepSpotDataLoader` | Class | PyTorch DataLoader for spot-level data with spatial preprocessing |
| `load_data()` | Function | Loads gene expression and image features from disk |
| `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()` | Function | Initializes foundation model and preprocessing transforms |
| `crop_tile()` | Function | Extracts image tiles at specified coordinates |
| `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()` | Function | End-to-end inference from image path to predicted expression |

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:74-93](), [README.md:21-22]()

---

## Workflow Stages Detail

### 1. Preprocessing ([see detailed guide](#7.1.1))

**Objectives:**
- Select 300-800 highly variable genes from spatial transcriptomics data
- Extract morphological features for each spot using foundation models
- Divide each spot into 9 non-overlapping mini-tiles (3×3 grid) to capture sub-spot heterogeneity
- Compute spatial neighbor graphs for context-aware modeling
- Generate grid coordinates for spots on H&E images

**Key Operations:**
- Gene selection based on variance ranking
- Per-spot feature extraction and storage as `.npy` files
- Mini-tile computation at spot_diameter/3 resolution
- Neighbor computation within specified radius (default: 1)

### 2. Training ([see detailed guide](#7.1.2))

**Objectives:**
- Initialize `DeepSpotDataLoader` with spatial upsampling and smoothing
- Configure `DeepSpot` model with appropriate context mode
- Train using MSE and/or Pearson correlation loss
- Save trained weights and configuration

**Key Operations:**
- Data normalization using StandardScaler
- Spatial upsampling to increase effective resolution
- Batch training with AdamW optimizer
- Model checkpoint saving

### 3. Inference ([see detailed guide](#7.1.3))

**Objectives:**
- Load pretrained weights (from Zenodo or custom training)
- Generate predictions on new H&E images
- Create AnnData objects compatible with scanpy/squidpy
- Visualize predicted spatial gene expression

**Key Operations:**
- On-the-fly feature extraction using `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()`
- Inverse scaling to original expression ranges
- Post-processing (e.g., negative value clipping)
- Spatial visualization

**Sources:** [README.md:60-78](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:1-511]()

---

## Data Flow Through Visium Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Files"
        A["H&E slide<br/>(.svs, .tiff)"]
        B["ST data<br/>(.h5ad)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Preprocessing Outputs"
        C["spot_embeddings/<br/>spot_0.npy<br/>spot_1.npy<br/>..."]
        D["gene_list.csv<br/>highly_variable_rank<br/>isPredicted"]
        E["coordinates.csv<br/>x_pixel, y_pixel<br/>x_array, y_array"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Artifacts"
        F["DeepSpotDataLoader<br/>batched tensors<br/>X: features<br/>y: expression"]
        G["final_model.pkl<br/>Phi modules<br/>Rho modules<br/>StandardScaler"]
        H["top_param_overall.yaml<br/>spot_diameter<br/>image_feature_model<br/>learning_rate"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inference Outputs"
        I["predicted_adata.h5ad<br/>.X: predictions<br/>.obs: metadata<br/>.obsm['spatial']"]
    end
    
    A --> C
    B --> D
    A --> E
    
    C --> F
    D --> F
    E --> F
    
    F --> G
    F --> H
    
    A --> I
    E --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I
    D --> I
```

**Diagram: Data artifacts and transformations in Visium workflow**

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:118-186]()

---

## Critical Configuration Parameters

The following parameters must be consistent across preprocessing, training, and inference stages:

| Parameter | Typical Value | Description | Impact |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|--------|
| `spot_diameter` | 100 pixels | Physical diameter of spot in H&E image at working resolution | Determines tile extraction size |
| `spot_distance` | 100 pixels | Center-to-center distance between adjacent spots | Controls grid density |
| `n_mini_tiles` | 9 | Number of sub-tiles per spot (always 3×3 grid) | Fixed architecture requirement |
| `image_feature_model` | `"uni"`, `"hoptimus0"`, `"phikon"` | Foundation model for feature extraction | Must match training model |
| `white_cutoff` | 200 | Mean RGB threshold for tissue detection (0-255) | Filters background spots |
| `neighbor_radius` | 1 | Radius for neighbor graph computation | Controls spatial context |
| `n_highly_variable_genes` | 300-800 | Number of genes to predict | Balances performance vs. coverage |
| `super_resolution` | `False` | Enable super-resolution mode during inference | Affects prediction granularity |

**Configuration Loading Example:**

```python
# Load training configuration for inference
with open('top_param_overall.yaml', 'r') as f:
    config = yaml.safe_load(f)
    
spot_diameter = config['spot_diameter']
image_feature_model = config['image_feature_model']
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:138-151]()

---

## Spot Context Modes

The `DeepSpot` model supports four spatial context modes, selectable during training and inference:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Context Mode Selection"
        Mode["DeepSpot<br/>forward()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Mode 1: Spot Only"
        M1["_forward_spot()<br/>Single spot tile<br/>No subspots<br/>No neighbors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Mode 2: Spot + Subspots"
        M2["_forward_spot_subspot()<br/>1 spot tile +<br/>9 mini-tiles (3x3)<br/>No neighbors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Mode 3: Spot + Neighbors"
        M3["_forward_spot_neighbors()<br/>1 spot tile +<br/>N neighbor spots<br/>No subspots"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Mode 4: Full Context"
        M4["_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors()<br/>1 spot tile +<br/>9 mini-tiles +<br/>N neighbor spots"]
    end
    
    Mode --> M1
    Mode --> M2
    Mode --> M3
    Mode --> M4
    
    M1 --> Phi["Phi Ensemble<br/>Feature Transform"]
    M2 --> Phi
    M3 --> Phi
    M4 --> Phi
    
    Phi --> Rho["Rho Ensemble<br/>Gene Prediction"]
```

**Diagram: DeepSpot context modes and neural layer routing**

Context selection impacts model capacity and inference speed. Mode 4 (full context) provides the most spatial information but requires more computation.

**Sources:** [README.md:33-38]()

---

## Integration with Pretrained Resources

### Pretrained DeepSpot Weights

Available from Zenodo for immediate inference without training:

```python
# Download from https://zenodo.org/records/15322099
model_weights = 'DeepSpot_pretrained_model_weights/Colon_HEST1K/final_model.pkl'
model_hparam = 'DeepSpot_pretrained_model_weights/Colon_HEST1K/top_param_overall.yaml'
gene_path = 'DeepSpot_pretrained_model_weights/Colon_HEST1K/info_highly_variable_genes.csv'

model = torch.load(model_weights, map_location=device)
model.eval()
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:33-46](), [README.md:75-78]()

### Foundation Model Integration

Foundation models must be downloaded separately and paths configured:

```python
# Example: UNI model
image_feature_model_path = "../huggingface/hub/models--MahmoodLab--UNI/blobs/..."

morphology_model, preprocess, feature_dim = get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(
    model_name='uni',
    device=device,
    model_path=image_feature_model_path
)
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:170-173](), [README.md:80-86]()

---

## Typical Workflow Execution

### Using Pretrained Models (Fast Track)

1. Download pretrained weights from Zenodo
2. Ensure foundation model weights are available
3. Load H&E image and generate spot coordinates
4. Run inference using `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()`
5. Inverse transform predictions to original scale
6. Visualize with squidpy

```python
counts = predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path(
    image_path,
    adata,
    spot_diameter,
    n_mini_tiles,
    preprocess,
    morphology_model,
    model_expression,
    device,
    super_resolution=False,
    neighbor_radius=1
)

counts = model_expression.inverse_transform(counts)
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:369-379]()

### Training Custom Models (Full Pipeline)

1. Preprocess spatial transcriptomics data and H&E images
2. Extract features for all spots and save as `.npy` files
3. Initialize `DeepSpotDataLoader` with spatial preprocessing
4. Train `DeepSpot` model with appropriate loss functions
5. Save model weights and configuration
6. Run inference on new samples using saved artifacts

---

## Output Structure

The final prediction is an AnnData object with the following structure:

```python
adata_predicted
# .X - Predicted gene expression matrix (n_spots, n_genes)
# .var - Gene metadata with gene names
# .obs - Spot metadata:
#        - x_pixel, y_pixel: pixel coordinates
#        - x_array, y_array: grid coordinates
#        - is_white: mean RGB value
#        - sampleID: sample identifier
#        - barcode: unique spot identifier
# .obsm['spatial'] - Spatial coordinates for visualization
# .uns['spatial']['library_id']['images']['hires'] - Downsampled H&E image
```

This structure is compatible with scanpy and squidpy for downstream analysis and visualization.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:273-314](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:433-439]()

# Page: Visium Preprocessing

# Visium Preprocessing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py](deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py)
- [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb)

</details>



This page documents the preprocessing steps required to prepare Visium spatial transcriptomics data for training DeepSpot models. Preprocessing transforms raw H&E histology images and gene expression data into model-ready features. For training procedures, see [Visium Training](#7.1.2). For inference with preprocessed data, see [Visium Inference](#7.1.3). For cell-level preprocessing in Xenium data, see [Xenium Preprocessing](#7.2.1).

---

## Overview

Visium preprocessing consists of five sequential stages that prepare data for model training:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Input Data"
        HE["H&E Whole-Slide Image<br/>.svs, .tiff, .jpg"]
        ST["Spatial Transcriptomics<br/>AnnData .h5ad"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 1: Gene Selection"
        HVG["select highly_variable_genes<br/>300-800 genes typical"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Spot Grid Generation"
        Grid["Generate spot coordinates<br/>x_pixel, y_pixel, x_array, y_array"]
        Tissue["Filter tissue spots<br/>white background detection"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Image Feature Extraction"
        Tiles["Extract spot tiles<br/>spot_diameter pixels"]
        MiniTiles["Divide into 3x3 mini-tiles<br/>n_mini_tiles=9"]
        Foundation["Foundation Model<br/>UNI/Hoptimus0/Phikon"]
        Features["Save features<br/>embeddings.npy"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 4: Neighbor Computation"
        Neighbors["compute_neighbors<br/>radius=1 default"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 5: Spatial Processing"
        Upsample["spatial_upsample_and_smooth<br/>clustering + resampling"]
        Normalize["log1p_normalization<br/>factor=10000"]
    end
    
    HE --> Grid
    ST --> HVG
    Grid --> Tissue
    Tissue --> Tiles
    Tiles --> MiniTiles
    MiniTiles --> Foundation
    Foundation --> Features
    Features --> Neighbors
    HVG --> Upsample
    Neighbors --> Upsample
    Upsample --> Normalize
    
    Normalize --> Output["Preprocessed Data<br/>Ready for DeepSpotDataLoader"]
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:132-174](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:213-257]()

---

## Gene Selection

Visium preprocessing begins with selecting highly variable genes (HVGs) from the spatial transcriptomics data. This reduces dimensionality and focuses model training on genes with meaningful expression variation.

### Selection Process

The system typically selects **300-800 genes** ranked by their variability across spots. The exact count depends on the tissue type and dataset characteristics. Gene selection is performed using scanpy's built-in functions and stored in the `.var` annotations of the AnnData object.

### Storage Format

Selected genes are stored in a CSV file with the following structure:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `gene_name` | Gene symbol (e.g., "MUC2", "ITLN1") |
| `highly_variable_rank` | Integer rank by variability |
| `isPredicted` | Boolean indicating if gene should be predicted |

The pretrained models include an `info_highly_variable_genes.csv` file that specifies which genes the model was trained to predict.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:181-185]()

---

## Spot Coordinate Generation

Spot coordinates define the spatial grid where predictions will be made. For Visium technology, spots are typically arranged in a hexagonal pattern with ~55μm diameter at 20x magnification.

### Grid Creation

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Image Dimensions"
        Image["pyvips.Image<br/>height x width"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Grid Parameters"
        SpotDiam["spot_diameter<br/>pixels at image resolution"]
        SpotDist["spot_distance<br/>spacing between centers"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Coordinate Generation"
        Loop["Iterate over image<br/>x: spot_diameter+1 to height-spot_diameter-1<br/>y: spot_diameter+1 to width-spot_diameter-1<br/>step: spot_distance"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output DataFrame"
        Coord["coord DataFrame<br/>x_array, y_array (grid indices)<br/>x_pixel, y_pixel (pixel coords)"]
    end
    
    Image --> Loop
    SpotDiam --> Loop
    SpotDist --> Loop
    Loop --> Coord
```

The coordinate generation creates a regular grid with four columns:
- `x_array`, `y_array`: Integer grid indices (0, 1, 2, ...)
- `x_pixel`, `y_pixel`: Pixel coordinates in the image

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:218-226]()

### Tissue Detection

Not all grid positions contain tissue. White background filtering identifies spots within tissue regions:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "For Each Spot"
        Extract["crop_tile from image<br/>center: x_pixel, y_pixel<br/>size: spot_diameter"]
        Mean["Calculate mean pixel intensity<br/>np.mean of RGB channels"]
        Compare["Compare to white_cutoff<br/>typical: 200"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Filtering"
        Filter["is_white_bool<br/>0 = tissue<br/>1 = background"]
        Keep["Keep spots where<br/>is_white_bool == 0"]
    end
    
    Extract --> Mean
    Mean --> Compare
    Compare --> Filter
    Filter --> Keep
```

Spots with mean intensity above `white_cutoff` (typically 200 for 8-bit RGB) are flagged as background and excluded from training.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:243-257]()

---

## Image Feature Extraction

Image feature extraction converts spot regions into numerical embeddings using pretrained pathology foundation models. This is the most computationally intensive preprocessing step.

### Spot-Level Feature Extraction

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Per Spot Processing"
        SpotImage["H&E image tile<br/>spot_diameter x spot_diameter"]
        MiniTile["Divide into n_mini_tiles=9<br/>3x3 non-overlapping grid"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Foundation Model Pipeline"
        Preprocess["Model-specific preprocessing<br/>resize, normalize, tensor conversion"]
        Model["Foundation Model Forward Pass<br/>UNI: 1024-dim<br/>Hoptimus0: 1536-dim<br/>Phikon: 768-dim"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Embedding["Feature vector per mini-tile<br/>Shape: (9, feature_dim)"]
        Save["Save to disk<br/>{out_folder}/data/image_features/<br/>{model_name}/{sample}.pkl"]
    end
    
    SpotImage --> MiniTile
    MiniTile --> Preprocess
    Preprocess --> Model
    Model --> Embedding
    Embedding --> Save
```

### Mini-Tile Decomposition

Each spot is divided into **9 non-overlapping mini-tiles** arranged in a 3×3 grid. This captures sub-spot spatial heterogeneity, which is critical since Visium spots (~55μm) typically contain 1-10 cells.

The mini-tile dimension calculation:
```
mini_tile_size = spot_diameter // 3
```

Each mini-tile is independently processed through the foundation model, producing 9 feature vectors per spot.

### Storage Structure

Preprocessed features are stored in pickle files organized by sample:

```
{out_folder}/data/
├── inputX/
│   └── {sample}.pkl          # Gene expression counts
└── image_features/
    └── {model_name}/
        └── {sample}.pkl      # Image embeddings
```

Each pickle file contains a pandas DataFrame indexed by barcode (spot identifier) with feature dimensions as columns.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:334-360](), [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:151-161]()

---

## Neighbor Computation

Neighbor computation identifies spatially adjacent spots to enable context-aware predictions. The `compute_neighbors` function finds spots within a specified radius.

### Neighbor Identification Algorithm

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input"
        Row["Spot coordinates<br/>x_array, y_array, sampleID"]
        Coords["All coordinates DataFrame"]
        Radius["radius parameter<br/>default=1"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Query Construction"
        Query["Range query:<br/>(x_array - radius) <= neighbor_x <= (x_array + radius)<br/>(y_array - radius) <= neighbor_y <= (y_array + radius)<br/>Same sampleID, exclude self"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Neighbors["String of neighbor barcodes<br/>joined by '___'"]
    end
    
    Row --> Query
    Coords --> Query
    Radius --> Query
    Query --> Neighbors
```

### Implementation Details

The `compute_neighbors` function at [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:112-121]() uses pandas query syntax to efficiently filter neighbors:

- **Radius**: Defines the grid distance (default `radius=1` includes immediate neighbors)
- **Same Sample**: Neighbors must be from the same tissue sample (`sampleID`)
- **Self-Exclusion**: The query spot itself is excluded
- **Output Format**: Neighbor barcodes concatenated with `"___"` delimiter

For a spot at position (10, 10) with radius=1, neighbors would be all spots at positions (9-11, 9-11) excluding (10, 10).

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:112-121]()

---

## Spatial Processing

Spatial processing applies optional augmentation and normalization techniques to improve model training stability and performance.

### Spatial Upsampling and Smoothing

The `spatial_upsample_and_smooth` function performs cluster-based upsampling to balance representation of tissue regions:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Per Sample Processing"
        Sample["Tissue sample<br/>spots + gene counts"]
        Cluster["Clustering<br/>PCA + Leiden/AESTETIK"]
        Balance["Balanced resampling<br/>equal spots per cluster"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional Smoothing"
        KNN["K-Nearest Neighbors<br/>smooth_n neighbors"]
        Smooth["Average gene expression<br/>across neighbors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parameters"
        Resolution["resolution: clustering granularity"]
        SmoothN["smooth_n: 0=off, >0=smoothing"]
        Augmentation["augmentation: 'default' or 'aestetik'"]
    end
    
    Sample --> Cluster
    Resolution --> Cluster
    Augmentation --> Cluster
    Cluster --> Balance
    Balance --> KNN
    SmoothN --> KNN
    KNN --> Smooth
```

**Key Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `resolution` | float | Leiden clustering resolution; higher = more clusters |
| `smooth_n` | int | Number of neighbors for smoothing; 0 disables |
| `augmentation` | str | `"default"` uses standard Leiden, `"aestetik"` uses AESTETIK |

The function returns:
1. Array of resampled barcodes (balanced across clusters)
2. Smoothed transcriptomics matrix (if `smooth_n > 0`)

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:65-98]()

### Normalization

Gene expression counts are normalized using log1p transformation to stabilize variance:

```python
# log1p_normalization formula
normalized = log(1 + ((counts / total_counts) * factor))
```

The `log1p_normalization` function at [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:128-129]():
- **Total Normalization**: Divides by spot total counts
- **Scaling**: Multiplies by `factor` (default 10000)
- **Log Transform**: Applies `log(1 + x)` to compress dynamic range

This is the standard scanpy normalization (`sc.pp.normalize_total` + `sc.pp.log1p`).

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:128-129]()

---

## Data Loading Interface

After preprocessing, the `load_data` function provides a unified interface to load gene expression and image features for model training.

### Function Signature

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Parameters"
        Samples["samples: list of sample IDs"]
        OutFolder["out_folder: base directory"]
        FeatureModel["feature_model: model name"]
        LoadImg["load_image_features: bool"]
        RawCounts["raw_counts: bool"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Loading Process"
        LoadExpr["Load gene expression<br/>{out_folder}/data/inputX/{sample}.pkl"]
        LoadFeats["Load image features<br/>{out_folder}/data/image_features/<br/>{feature_model}/{sample}.pkl"]
        Norm["Optional normalization<br/>log1p_normalization if not raw_counts"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Dictionary"
        Output["dict with keys:<br/>'y': gene expression<br/>'X': image features<br/>'barcode': spot identifiers"]
    end
    
    Samples --> LoadExpr
    OutFolder --> LoadExpr
    LoadExpr --> LoadFeats
    FeatureModel --> LoadFeats
    LoadImg --> LoadFeats
    LoadFeats --> Norm
    RawCounts --> Norm
    Norm --> Output
```

### Return Structure

The function returns a dictionary with three keys:

| Key | Type | Shape | Description |
|-----|------|-------|-------------|
| `"y"` | np.ndarray | (n_spots, n_genes) | Gene expression matrix, normalized unless `raw_counts=True` |
| `"X"` | pd.DataFrame | (n_spots, feature_dim) | Image feature embeddings, only if `load_image_features=True` |
| `"barcode"` | np.ndarray | (n_spots,) | Spot identifiers in format `"{sample_id}_{spot_id}"` |

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:132-174]()

## Complete Preprocessing Workflow

The following diagram shows how preprocessing components interact in a typical workflow:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Configuration"
        Config["User Configuration<br/>spot_diameter, spot_distance<br/>feature_model, n_hvgs<br/>out_folder"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 1: Gene Selection"
        LoadAnnData["Load AnnData<br/>raw counts"]
        SelectHVG["sc.pp.highly_variable_genes<br/>n_top_genes=300-800"]
        SaveGenes["Save gene list<br/>info_highly_variable_genes.csv"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 2: Coordinate Generation"
        GenGrid["Generate coordinate grid<br/>based on image dimensions"]
        FilterWhite["Filter white background<br/>crop_tile + intensity check"]
        SaveCoord["Save coordinates<br/>as AnnData.obs metadata"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 3: Feature Extraction"
        LoadFoundation["Load foundation model<br/>get_morphology_model_and_preprocess"]
        ExtractLoop["For each spot:<br/>1. Crop tile<br/>2. Divide into 9 mini-tiles<br/>3. Extract features"]
        SaveFeatures["Save features<br/>{out_folder}/data/image_features/<br/>{model}/{sample}.pkl"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 4: Neighbor + Spatial Processing"
        ComputeNeigh["compute_neighbors<br/>radius=1"]
        SpatialProc["spatial_upsample_and_smooth<br/>clustering + balancing"]
        SaveExpr["Save processed expression<br/>{out_folder}/data/inputX/<br/>{sample}.pkl"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 5: Training Data Loading"
        LoadData["load_data function<br/>combines all preprocessed data"]
        DataLoader["DeepSpotDataLoader<br/>ready for training"]
    end
    
    Config --> LoadAnnData
    LoadAnnData --> SelectHVG
    SelectHVG --> SaveGenes
    
    Config --> GenGrid
    GenGrid --> FilterWhite
    FilterWhite --> SaveCoord
    
    Config --> LoadFoundation
    SaveCoord --> ExtractLoop
    LoadFoundation --> ExtractLoop
    ExtractLoop --> SaveFeatures
    
    SaveCoord --> ComputeNeigh
    SaveGenes --> SpatialProc
    ComputeNeigh --> SpatialProc
    SpatialProc --> SaveExpr
    
    SaveFeatures --> LoadData
    SaveExpr --> LoadData
    LoadData --> DataLoader
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:132-174](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb]()

## Preprocessing Output Summary

After completing all preprocessing steps, the following directory structure is created:

```
{out_folder}/
├── data/
│   ├── inputX/
│   │   └── {sample}.pkl                    # Normalized gene expression
│   └── image_features/
│       └── {feature_model}/
│           └── {sample}.pkl                # Image embeddings (9 per spot)
└── models/
    └── {experiment_name}/
        └── info_highly_variable_genes.csv  # Gene metadata
```

### File Formats

- **Gene Expression** (`inputX/{sample}.pkl`): Pandas DataFrame with barcode index, gene columns
- **Image Features** (`image_features/{model}/{sample}.pkl`): Pandas DataFrame with barcode index, feature dimension columns
- **Gene Metadata** (`info_highly_variable_genes.csv`): CSV with columns `gene_name`, `highly_variable_rank`, `isPredicted`

These files are consumed by `load_data` and passed to `DeepSpotDataLoader` for model training (see [Visium Training](#7.1.2)).

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:144-161]()

# Page: Visium Training

# Visium Training

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot/cell/model.py](deepspot/cell/model.py)
- [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb)

</details>



This page documents the process of training DeepSpot models on Visium spatial transcriptomics data. Training involves configuring a `DeepSpotDataLoader`, initializing a `DeepSpot` model with appropriate hyperparameters, and running the training loop using PyTorch Lightning. After preprocessing (see [Visium Preprocessing](#7.1.1)), the training stage learns the mapping from H&E image features to gene expression counts. For using pre-trained models or performing inference, see [Visium Inference](#7.1.3).

## Training Pipeline Overview

The Visium training workflow follows a standard supervised learning pattern, utilizing preprocessed image features and gene expression data to train the DeepSpot neural network.

**Training Pipeline Architecture**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Preprocessed Data"
        ImgFeatures["Image Features<br/>(embeddings.npy files)"]
        GeneData["Gene Expression<br/>(AnnData .h5ad)"]
        HVGs["Highly Variable Genes<br/>(300-800 selected)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Loading"
        Loader["DeepSpotDataLoader"]
        SpatialProc["Spatial Processing<br/>upsampling, smoothing,<br/>neighbor computation"]
        Scaler["StandardScaler<br/>(fit on training data)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Architecture"
        DeepSpotModel["DeepSpot"]
        PhiModules["Phi Ensemble<br/>(10 modules)"]
        RhoModules["Rho Ensemble<br/>(10 modules)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Loop"
        Forward["Forward Pass<br/>(_forward_spot_*)"]
        LossCalc["Loss Computation<br/>(MSE, Pearson, etc.)"]
        Backward["Backward Pass<br/>(gradient computation)"]
        OptStep["AdamW Optimizer Step"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        Checkpoint["Model Checkpoint<br/>(.pkl or .ckpt)"]
        HParams["Hyperparameters<br/>(.yaml)"]
        ScalerFile["Fitted Scaler<br/>(for inference)"]
    end
    
    ImgFeatures --> Loader
    GeneData --> Loader
    HVGs --> Loader
    
    Loader --> SpatialProc
    SpatialProc --> Scaler
    Scaler --> DeepSpotModel
    
    DeepSpotModel --> PhiModules
    PhiModules --> RhoModules
    
    DeepSpotModel --> Forward
    Forward --> LossCalc
    LossCalc --> Backward
    Backward --> OptStep
    OptStep --> DeepSpotModel
    
    DeepSpotModel --> Checkpoint
    DeepSpotModel --> HParams
    Scaler --> ScalerFile
```

Sources: [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:1-510]()

## DeepSpotDataLoader Configuration

The `DeepSpotDataLoader` batches preprocessed data and applies spatial transformations required for training. It handles spot-level data organization and prepares inputs for the four context modes supported by DeepSpot.

### Initialization Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `data_path` | str | Required | Path to preprocessed data directory |
| `split` | str | Required | Dataset split: 'train', 'val', or 'test' |
| `batch_size` | int | 32 | Number of spots per batch |
| `num_workers` | int | 0 | DataLoader workers for parallel loading |
| `spot_context` | str | 'spot_subspot_neighbors' | Context mode (see below) |
| `neighbor_radius` | int | 1 | Radius for neighbor computation |
| `use_upsampling` | bool | True | Apply spatial upsampling to gene counts |
| `use_smoothing` | bool | True | Apply spatial smoothing to gene counts |
| `scaler` | object | None | sklearn scaler for normalization (fit on training set) |

### Spot Context Modes

DeepSpot supports four spatial context configurations:

| Mode | Description | Input Structure |
|------|-------------|-----------------|
| `'spot'` | Individual spot only | Single tile (1 × feature_dim) |
| `'spot_subspot'` | Spot with 9 mini-tiles | 9 tiles (9 × feature_dim) |
| `'spot_neighbors'` | Spot with neighbor spots | Spot + neighbors |
| `'spot_subspot_neighbors'` | Full context | 9 mini-tiles + neighbor spots |

The context mode must match the forward function used during model initialization (see Model Initialization section).

**DataLoader Initialization Example**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Training Split"
        TrainData["train/*.npy<br/>train_adata.h5ad"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DeepSpotDataLoader"
        Init["__init__()"]
        Params["batch_size=32<br/>spot_context='spot_subspot_neighbors'<br/>neighbor_radius=1<br/>use_upsampling=True"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Preprocessing"
        Upsample["spatial_upsampling()"]
        Smooth["spatial_smoothing()"]
        Neighbors["get_neighbors()"]
        Scale["StandardScaler.transform()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Batch Output"
        Batch["X: [batch, features]<br/>y: [batch, n_genes]"]
    end
    
    TrainData --> Init
    Params --> Init
    Init --> Upsample
    Upsample --> Smooth
    Smooth --> Neighbors
    Neighbors --> Scale
    Scale --> Batch
```

Sources: [deepspot/spot/dataloader.py]() (inferred from architecture), [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py]() (inferred from preprocessing utilities)

## Model Initialization

The `DeepSpot` class inherits from `L.LightningModule` and encapsulates the ensemble architecture with Phi and Rho neural layers. Initialization requires careful configuration of hyperparameters that define network capacity, regularization, and spatial context handling.

### Core Hyperparameters

**DeepSpot Initialization Parameters**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Architecture Parameters"
        InputSize["input_size<br/>(foundation model dim)<br/>1024 for UNI<br/>1536 for Hoptimus0<br/>768 for Phikon"]
        OutputSize["output_size<br/>(number of HVGs)<br/>300-800 genes"]
        Phi2Rho["phi2rho_size<br/>(intermediate dim)<br/>typically 1024"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ensemble Configuration"
        NEnsemble["n_ensemble=10<br/>or separate:<br/>n_ensemble_phi<br/>n_ensemble_rho"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Regularization"
        Dropout["p=0.2<br/>or separate:<br/>p_phi<br/>p_rho"]
        WeightDecay["weight_decay=1e-6"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training"
        LR["lr=1e-4"]
        LossFunc["loss_func='mse'<br/>or 'pearson', 'mse_pearson',<br/>'cosine', 'l1', 'huber'"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Spatial Context"
        SpotContext["spot_context<br/>'spot'<br/>'spot_subspot'<br/>'spot_neighbors'<br/>'spot_subspot_neighbors'"]
        AggNeighbors["agg_neighbors='max'<br/>or 'mean', 'sum'"]
    end
    
    InputSize --> DeepSpot["DeepSpot()"]
    OutputSize --> DeepSpot
    Phi2Rho --> DeepSpot
    NEnsemble --> DeepSpot
    Dropout --> DeepSpot
    WeightDecay --> DeepSpot
    LR --> DeepSpot
    LossFunc --> DeepSpot
    SpotContext --> DeepSpot
    AggNeighbors --> DeepSpot
```

### Loss Function Selection

The `loss_func` parameter determines the training objective. The model maps these string identifiers to corresponding loss implementations:

| loss_func Value | Implementation | Use Case |
|-----------------|----------------|----------|
| `"mse"` | `loss_mse_function` | Standard regression |
| `"pearson"` | `loss_pearson_function` | Correlation-based |
| `"mse_pearson"` | `loss_mse_pearson_function` | Combined MSE + correlation |
| `"cos"` | `loss_cosine_function` | Cosine similarity |
| `"mse_cos"` | `loss_mse_cosine_function` | MSE + cosine |
| `"l1"` | `loss_l1_function` | L1 regression |
| `"l1_cos"` | `loss_l1_cosine_function` | L1 + cosine |
| `"huber"` | `loss_huber_function` | Robust regression |
| `"huber_cos"` | `loss_huber_cosine_function` | Huber + cosine |
| `"poisson"` | `loss_poisson_function` | Count data distribution |

Loss function mapping occurs in [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]() (DeepSpot follows identical pattern).

### Scaler Integration

The `scaler` parameter accepts a fitted sklearn preprocessing object (typically `StandardScaler`) that was fit on the training set during preprocessing. This scaler is stored with the model and used for:

1. **During Training**: The dataloader applies `scaler.transform()` to gene counts before feeding to the model
2. **During Inference**: The model's `inverse_transform()` method converts normalized predictions back to original scale

**Critical**: The same scaler instance must be used during training and inference, or predictions will be incorrectly scaled.

Sources: [deepspot/cell/model.py:63-128](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:138-151]()

## Training Configuration with PyTorch Lightning

DeepSpot leverages PyTorch Lightning's `Trainer` for orchestrating the training loop. The trainer handles device management, gradient computation, logging, and checkpointing.

### Trainer Initialization

**Lightning Trainer Configuration**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Hardware"
        Accelerator["accelerator='gpu'<br/>or 'cpu'"]
        Devices["devices=1<br/>(single GPU)"]
        Precision["precision=32<br/>or 16 for mixed precision"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Control"
        MaxEpochs["max_epochs=100"]
        GradClip["gradient_clip_val=1.0"]
        DetOverfit["detect_anomaly=False"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Checkpointing"
        Callback["ModelCheckpoint<br/>monitor='val'<br/>save_top_k=1<br/>mode='min'"]
        SaveDir["default_root_dir<br/>(checkpoint directory)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logging"
        Logger["logger=TensorBoardLogger<br/>or CSVLogger"]
        LogEvery["log_every_n_steps=50"]
    end
    
    Accelerator --> Trainer["L.Trainer()"]
    Devices --> Trainer
    Precision --> Trainer
    MaxEpochs --> Trainer
    GradClip --> Trainer
    DetOverfit --> Trainer
    Callback --> Trainer
    SaveDir --> Trainer
    Logger --> Trainer
    LogEvery --> Trainer
```

### Training Loop Execution

The training loop is executed by calling `trainer.fit()` with the model and dataloaders:

**Training Execution Flow**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Trainer as "L.Trainer"
    participant Model as "DeepSpot"
    participant TrainLoader as "train_dataloader"
    participant ValLoader as "val_dataloader"
    participant Optimizer as "AdamW"
    
    Trainer->>TrainLoader: get batch
    TrainLoader-->>Trainer: X, y
    Trainer->>Model: training_step(batch)
    Model->>Model: forward(X)
    Model->>Model: loss_func(y_hat, y)
    Model-->>Trainer: loss
    Trainer->>Optimizer: zero_grad()
    Trainer->>Optimizer: loss.backward()
    Trainer->>Optimizer: step()
    
    Note over Trainer,ValLoader: After N training steps
    
    Trainer->>ValLoader: get batch
    ValLoader-->>Trainer: X_val, y_val
    Trainer->>Model: validation_step(batch)
    Model->>Model: forward(X_val)
    Model->>Model: loss_func(y_hat_val, y_val)
    Model-->>Trainer: val_loss
    Trainer->>Trainer: log metrics
    Trainer->>Trainer: save checkpoint (if best)
```

The core training lifecycle is implemented in:
- [deepspot/cell/model.py:144-168]() - `loop_step`, `training_step`, `validation_step` methods
- [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218]() - `configure_optimizers` returning AdamW

Sources: [deepspot/cell/model.py:144-218]()

## Hyperparameter Configuration Files

Training configurations are typically stored in YAML files for reproducibility and easy modification. The pretrained models include these configuration files alongside the model weights.

### YAML Configuration Structure

```yaml
# Model architecture
input_size: 1024
output_size: 500
phi2rho_size: 1024
n_ensemble: 10

# Regularization
p: 0.2
weight_decay: 1e-6

# Training
lr: 1e-4
loss_func: "mse_pearson"
random_seed: 2024

# Spatial context
spot_context: "spot_subspot_neighbors"
agg_neighbors: "max"
neighbor_radius: 1

# Data processing
use_upsampling: true
use_smoothing: true

# Image features
image_feature_model: "uni"
spot_diameter: 100
spot_distance: 100
n_mini_tiles: 9
```

**Configuration Loading Pattern**

```mermaid

    YAMLFile["config.yaml"]

    ConfigDict["config dict"]
    
    ModelInit["DeepSpot(**config)"]
    TrainerInit["L.Trainer(...)"]
    LoaderInit["DeepSpotDataLoader(**config)"]
    
    YAMLFile --> LoadYAML
    LoadYAML --> ConfigDict
    ConfigDict --> ModelInit
    ConfigDict --> TrainerInit
    ConfigDict --> LoaderInit
```

## Model Training Workflow

The complete training workflow integrates all components from data loading through model checkpointing.

### Complete Training Pipeline

**End-to-End Training Code Flow**

```mermaid

    subgraph "1. Data Preparation"

    end

    end

    end

        Fit["trainer.fit<br/>(model, train_loader, val_loader)"]
    end

    end
    
    LoadConfig --> TrainLoader
```

### Training Monitoring

The model tracks training and validation loss internally for visualization:

- `model.training_loss` - List of per-step training losses
- `model.validation_loss` - List of per-step validation losses
- `model.plot_loss()` - Visualizes smoothed loss curves

The loss plotting implementation: [deepspot/cell/model.py:220-281]()

### Model Checkpointing

Model weights can be saved in two formats:

1. **Full Model**: `torch.save(model, 'model.pkl')` - Saves entire model object
2. **State Dict**: `torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'model_weights.pth')` - Saves only parameters
3. **Lightning Checkpoint**: `trainer.save_checkpoint('model.ckpt')` - Includes optimizer state

For inference, the full model approach is simplest as it preserves the scaler and all hyperparameters. This is demonstrated in [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:344-346]():

```python
model_expression = torch.load(model_weights, map_location=device)
model_expression.to(device)
model_expression.eval()
```

Sources: [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:344-346]()

## Training Best Practices

### Recommended Hyperparameter Ranges

| Hyperparameter | Recommended Range | Notes |
|----------------|-------------------|-------|
| `lr` | 1e-5 to 1e-3 | Start with 1e-4 |
| `batch_size` | 16 to 128 | Limited by GPU memory |
| `n_ensemble` | 5 to 15 | 10 is default, higher = slower but more robust |
| `p` (dropout) | 0.1 to 0.3 | Regularization strength |
| `phi2rho_size` | 512 to 2048 | Intermediate representation size |
| `weight_decay` | 1e-7 to 1e-5 | AdamW regularization |

### Context Mode Selection

- **`spot`**: Fast, limited spatial information (baseline)
- **`spot_subspot`**: Captures sub-spot heterogeneity (recommended for Visium)
- **`spot_neighbors`**: Incorporates spatial neighborhood context
- **`spot_subspot_neighbors`**: Full spatial context (highest accuracy, slowest training)

### Loss Function Guidelines

- **Start with `"mse"`** for baseline performance
- **Use `"mse_pearson"`** for better correlation with ground truth
- **Try `"huber"`** if data has outliers
- **Experiment with cosine variants** for normalized expression patterns

### Reproducibility

To ensure reproducible training:

1. Set `random_seed` in `DeepSpot.__init__()` (calls `fix_seed()`)
2. Use deterministic algorithms: `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`
3. Set `cudnn.benchmark = False` in [deepspot/cell/model.py:3]()
4. Save the exact configuration YAML used for training

The `fix_seed()` utility is referenced in [deepspot/cell/model.py:86]()

Sources: [deepspot/cell/model.py:78-86](), [deepspot/utils/utils.py]() (inferred for `fix_seed`)

# Visium Inference

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py](deepspot/utils/utils_image.py)
- [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the inference workflow for predicting spatial transcriptomics gene expression from H&E histology images using trained DeepSpot models. Inference can be performed using either pre-trained weights downloaded from Zenodo or custom weights from a training run.

For preprocessing steps to prepare data before inference, see [Visium Preprocessing](#7.1.1). For training custom DeepSpot models, see [Visium Training](#7.1.2). For cell-level inference on Xenium data, see [Xenium Inference](#7.2.3).

---

## Overview

The Visium inference workflow consists of five stages:

1. **Setup**: Load pre-trained model weights, configuration parameters, and gene lists
2. **Coordinate Generation**: Create a grid of spot coordinates covering the H&E image
3. **Tissue Detection**: Filter spots to retain only those within tissue regions
4. **Prediction**: Extract image features and predict gene expression for each spot
5. **Post-processing**: Transform predictions back to original scale and create output AnnData

**Diagram: Visium Inference Pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Input Stage"
        Weights["Pre-trained Weights<br/>final_model.pkl"]
        Config["Hyperparameters<br/>top_param_overall.yaml"]
        Genes["Gene List<br/>info_highly_variable_genes.csv"]
        Image["H&E Image<br/>.jpg, .svs, .tiff"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Coordinate Generation"
        GridGen["Generate Spot Grid<br/>based on spot_diameter<br/>and spot_distance"]
        TissueFilter["Filter Tissue Spots<br/>using white_cutoff<br/>threshold"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Initialization"
        LoadDeepSpot["Load DeepSpot Model<br/>torch.load(model_weights)"]
        LoadFoundation["Load Foundation Model<br/>get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inference Execution"
        PredictFunc["predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()"]
        ExtractTiles["Extract Tiles<br/>crop_tile()<br/>compute_mini_tiles()"]
        ComputeNeigh["Compute Neighbors<br/>compute_neighbors()"]
        ExtractFeatures["Extract Features<br/>morphology_model()"]
        Predict["Predict Expression<br/>model_expression()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-processing"
        InverseTransform["Rescale Predictions<br/>model.inverse_transform()"]
        Cleanup["Clean Negative Values<br/>counts[counts < 0] = 0"]
        CreateAnnData["Create AnnData Object<br/>with predictions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        AnnDataOut["AnnData with Predictions<br/>adata.X = predicted_counts"]
        Visualize["Visualize with squidpy<br/>sq.pl.spatial_scatter()"]
    end
    
    Weights --> LoadDeepSpot
    Config --> LoadDeepSpot
    Genes --> CreateAnnData
    Image --> GridGen
    
    GridGen --> TissueFilter
    TissueFilter --> PredictFunc
    
    LoadDeepSpot --> PredictFunc
    LoadFoundation --> PredictFunc
    
    PredictFunc --> ExtractTiles
    PredictFunc --> ComputeNeigh
    ExtractTiles --> ExtractFeatures
    ComputeNeigh --> ExtractFeatures
    ExtractFeatures --> Predict
    
    Predict --> InverseTransform
    InverseTransform --> Cleanup
    Cleanup --> CreateAnnData
    
    CreateAnnData --> AnnDataOut
    AnnDataOut --> Visualize
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:1-510](), [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:241-293]()

## Prerequisites

Before running inference, ensure the following are available:

| Requirement | Description | Location |
|-------------|-------------|----------|
| **Pre-trained Weights** | DeepSpot model checkpoint (`.pkl` file) | Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/15322099 |
| **Configuration File** | Model hyperparameters (`.yaml` file) | Included with pre-trained weights |
| **Gene List** | CSV with highly variable genes to predict | Included with pre-trained weights |
| **Foundation Model Weights** | Pathology foundation model (UNI, Hoptimus0, Phikon) | HuggingFace (see [Foundation Models](#3.3)) |
| **H&E Image** | Histology image for prediction target | User-provided (`.jpg`, `.svs`, `.tiff`) |

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:33-56](), [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:120-151]()

## Downloading Pre-trained Weights

Pre-trained DeepSpot models are available on Zenodo. The weights archive contains three critical files:

```python
# Download and extract weights

!unzip DeepSpot_pretrained_model_weights.zip
```

```
DeepSpot_pretrained_model_weights/
├── Colon_HEST1K/
│   ├── final_model.pkl              # DeepSpot model weights
│   ├── top_param_overall.yaml       # Hyperparameters
│   └── info_highly_variable_genes.csv  # Gene list with prediction flags
```

## Configuration Parameters

Load the model configuration from the YAML file to extract critical parameters:

```python
import yaml

with open(model_hparam, "r") as stream:
    config = yaml.safe_load(stream)

# Key parameters
spot_diameter = config['spot_diameter']      # Spot diameter in pixels (e.g., 100)
spot_distance = config['spot_distance']      # Distance between spots (e.g., 100)
image_feature_model = config['image_feature_model']  # Foundation model name (e.g., "uni")
n_mini_tiles = 9                             # Always 9 for Visium (3×3 grid)
```

**Important Parameters:**

| Parameter | Description | Typical Value |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| `spot_diameter` | Diameter of each spot in pixels at the H&E image resolution | 100 (for 20× magnification) |
| `spot_distance` | Spacing between adjacent spot centers | 100 (for 20× magnification) |
| `n_mini_tiles` | Number of sub-tiles per spot (always 3×3 for Visium) | 9 |
| `image_feature_model` | Foundation model identifier | `"uni"`, `"hoptimus0"`, `"phikon"` |

**Note:** The `spot_diameter` and `spot_distance` values depend on the H&E image magnification. For 20× magnification imaging Visium tissue (55 μm spot diameter, 100 μm center-to-center), typical values are 100 pixels each. Adjust these parameters based on your specific imaging resolution.

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:138-151]()

| `isPredicted` | Boolean flag indicating if gene is predicted |
| `highly_variable_rank` | Rank of gene in highly variable gene selection |

## Generating Spot Coordinates

Create a regular grid of spot coordinates covering the entire H&E image:

**Diagram: Spot Coordinate Generation Process**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input"
        ImageFile["H&E Image<br/>pyvips.Image"]
        SpotDiam["spot_diameter<br/>(e.g., 100 pixels)"]
        SpotDist["spot_distance<br/>(e.g., 100 pixels)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Grid Generation"
        IterateX["Iterate X:<br/>spot_diameter+1 to<br/>height-spot_diameter-1<br/>step: spot_distance"]
        IterateY["Iterate Y:<br/>spot_diameter+1 to<br/>width-spot_diameter-1<br/>step: spot_distance"]
        CreateCoord["Create DataFrame:<br/>x_array, y_array,<br/>x_pixel, y_pixel"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        CoordDF["Coordinate DataFrame<br/>with spot positions"]
    end
    
    ImageFile --> IterateX
    SpotDiam --> IterateX
    SpotDist --> IterateX
    
    ImageFile --> IterateY
    SpotDiam --> IterateY
    SpotDist --> IterateY
    
    IterateX --> CreateCoord
    IterateY --> CreateCoord
    CreateCoord --> CoordDF
```

```python
import pyvips

image = pyvips.Image.new_from_file(image_path)

coord = []
for i, x in enumerate(range(spot_diameter + 1, 
                            image.height - spot_diameter - 1, 
                            spot_distance)):
    for j, y in enumerate(range(spot_diameter + 1, 
                                image.width - spot_diameter - 1, 
                                spot_distance)):
        coord.append([i, j, x, y])

coord = pd.DataFrame(coord, columns=['x_array', 'y_array', 'x_pixel', 'y_pixel'])
coord.index = coord.index.astype(str)
```

The resulting DataFrame contains:
- `x_array`, `y_array`: Grid indices (0-indexed)
- `x_pixel`, `y_pixel`: Pixel coordinates in the image

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:218-226]()

---

## Tissue Detection and Filtering

Filter spots to retain only those within tissue regions using a white threshold:

```python
from deepspot.utils.utils_image import crop_tile
from tqdm import tqdm

is_white = []
for _, row in tqdm(coord.iterrows()):
    x = row.x_pixel - int(spot_diameter // 2)
    y = row.y_pixel - int(spot_diameter // 2)
    
    main_tile = crop_tile(image, x, y, spot_diameter)
    main_tile = main_tile[:,:,:3]  # RGB channels only
    white = np.mean(main_tile)
    is_white.append(white)

coord['is_white'] = is_white
coord['is_white_bool'] = (coord['is_white'] > white_cutoff).astype(int)

# Filter to tissue spots only
coord_tissue = coord[coord.is_white_bool == 0]
```

**White Cutoff Parameter:**
- Typical value: `white_cutoff = 200` (on 0-255 scale)
- Higher values = more strict filtering (removes lighter spots)
- Lower values = more permissive (includes more spots)

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:243-257](), [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:190-198]()

---

## Creating the AnnData Object

Prepare an empty AnnData object to hold predictions:

```python
import anndata as ad
import numpy as np

# Initialize empty count matrix
counts = np.empty((len(coord_tissue), selected_genes_bool.sum()))

# Create AnnData
adata = ad.AnnData(counts)
adata.var.index = genes[selected_genes_bool].gene_name.values
adata.obs = adata.obs.merge(coord_tissue, left_index=True, right_index=True)
adata.obs['sampleID'] = sample
adata.obs['barcode'] = adata.obs.index
```

**Sources:** [example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb:274-283]()

```python
import torch
from deepspot.utils.utils_image import get_morphology_model_and_preprocess

# Set device
device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')

# Load DeepSpot model
model_expression = torch.load(model_weights, map_location=device)
model_expression.to(device)
model_expression.eval()

# Load foundation model
morphology_model, preprocess, feature_dim = get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(
    model_name=image_feature_model,
    device=device,
    model_path=image_feature_model_path
)
morphology_model.to(device)
morphology_model.eval()
```

**Foundation Model Options:**

| Model Name | Feature Dimension | Path Requirements |
|------------|------------------|-------------------|
| `"uni"` | 1024 | Path to UNI weights from HuggingFace |
| `"hoptimus0"` | 1536 | Path to Hoptimus0 weights from HuggingFace |
| `"phikon"` | 768 | Path to Phikon model directory |
| `"inception"` | 2048 | Uses torchvision weights (no path needed) |

## Running Inference

Execute the prediction using `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path`:
