# deepspot.spot

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md](.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md)
- [deepspot/cell/model.py](deepspot/cell/model.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides API-level reference documentation for the `deepspot.spot` module, which contains all components for spot-level spatial transcriptomics prediction. The module includes:

- `DeepSpot` - the main neural network model for spot-level predictions
- `DeepSpotDataLoader` - data loader for batching spot features and gene counts
- Loss functions - various loss functions for training spot models
- `Phi` and `Rho` - neural network building blocks used in the DeepSpot architecture

For comprehensive workflow guides using these components, see [Visium Spot Workflow](#7.1). For conceptual explanations of the deep-set architecture, see [Deep-Set Architecture](#3.2). For detailed model architecture discussion, see [DeepSpot Model](#5.2).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:1-113]()

---

## Module Overview

The following diagram shows the relationship between components in the `deepspot.spot` module:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "deepspot.spot Module"
        DeepSpot["DeepSpot<br/>(model.py)"]
        DataLoader["DeepSpotDataLoader<br/>(dataloader.py)"]
        LossFuncs["Loss Functions<br/>(loss.py)"]
        Phi["Phi Layer<br/>(model.py)"]
        Rho["Rho Layer<br/>(model.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        Lightning["lightning.LightningModule"]
        PyTorch["torch.nn.Module"]
        TorchDataset["torch.utils.data.Dataset"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Flow"
        InputData["Spot Features<br/>+ Gene Counts"]
        Predictions["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    end
    
    DeepSpot --> Phi
    DeepSpot --> Rho
    DeepSpot --> LossFuncs
    DataLoader --> InputData
    InputData --> DeepSpot
    DeepSpot --> Predictions
    
    DeepSpot -.->|"inherits from"| Lightning
    Phi -.->|"inherits from"| PyTorch
    Rho -.->|"inherits from"| PyTorch
    DataLoader -.->|"inherits from"| TorchDataset
    
    Lightning -.->|"uses"| PyTorch
```

**Figure 1: deepspot.spot Module Components**

The module follows a layered architecture where `DeepSpot` orchestrates training and inference, `Phi` and `Rho` layers provide the core neural transformations, `DeepSpotDataLoader` handles data batching, and loss functions quantify prediction quality.

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:43-62]()

## DeepSpot Model Class

### Class Definition

The `DeepSpot` class is the main model for spot-level spatial transcriptomics prediction, inheriting from `lightning.LightningModule`.

**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:58-217]()

### Initialization Parameters

The `DeepSpot.__init__` method accepts the following parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_size` | `int` | - | Dimension of input features (e.g., 1024 for UNI embeddings) |
| `output_size` | `int` | - | Number of genes to predict |
| `loss_func` | `str` | `"mse"` | Loss function name: `"mse"`, `"pearson"`, `"cos"`, `"l1"`, `"huber"`, `"mse_cos"`, `"l1_cos"`, `"huber_cos"`, `"mse_pearson"`, `"poisson"` |
| `lr` | `float` | `1e-4` | Learning rate for AdamW optimizer |
| `p` | `float` | `0.2` | Default dropout probability |
| `p_phi` | `float` | `None` | Dropout probability for Phi layers (overrides `p` if set) |
| `p_rho` | `float` | `None` | Dropout probability for Rho layers (overrides `p` if set) |
| `n_ensemble` | `int` | `10` | Default number of ensemble modules |
| `n_ensemble_phi` | `int` | `None` | Number of Phi ensemble modules (overrides `n_ensemble` if set) |
| `n_ensemble_rho` | `int` | `None` | Number of Rho ensemble modules (overrides `n_ensemble` if set) |
| `phi2rho_size` | `int` | `1024` | Hidden dimension size between Phi and Rho stages |
| `emb_size` | `int` | `1024` | Embedding size (deprecated parameter) |
| `weight_decay` | `float` | `1e-6` | Weight decay for AdamW optimizer |
| `random_seed` | `int` | `2024` | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `agg_neighbors` | `str` | `"max"` | Aggregation operation for neighbor features: `"max"`, `"mean"`, `"sum"` |
| `scaler` | `object` | `None` | Optional sklearn scaler for inverse transformation |
| `spot_context` | `str` | `"spot_subspot_neighbors"` | Spot context mode (see Spot Context Modes section) |

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:59-108](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:64-128]()

### Spot Context Modes

The `DeepSpot` model supports four spot context modes, each using different spatial information:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "spot_context modes"
        mode1["'spot'<br/>Single spot features"]
        mode2["'spot_subspot'<br/>Spot + 9 mini-tiles"]
        mode3["'spot_neighbors'<br/>Spot + neighbor spots"]
        mode4["'spot_subspot_neighbors'<br/>All: spot + mini-tiles + neighbors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Forward Methods"
        fw1["_forward_spot()"]
        fw2["_forward_spot_subspot()"]
        fw3["_forward_spot_neighbors()"]
        fw4["_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phi Multiplier"
        mult1["1x"]
        mult2["2x"]
        mult3["2x"]
        mult4["3x"]
    end
    
    mode1 --> fw1
    mode2 --> fw2
    mode3 --> fw3
    mode4 --> fw4
    
    fw1 --> mult1
    fw2 --> mult2
    fw3 --> mult3
    fw4 --> mult4
```

**Figure 2: Spot Context Modes and Their Forward Methods**

The context mode determines:
1. Which forward method is called during inference
2. The Phi multiplier, which affects the size of the concatenated feature vector passed to Rho layers

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-126](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:54-57]()

### Forward Pass Methods

Each spot context mode has a corresponding forward method:

#### `_forward_spot(x)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-165]()

Processes a single spot's features without spatial context.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["x: spot features<br/>(batch_size, input_size)"]
    PhiApp["_apply_phi()<br/>operation=NONE"]
    RhoApp["_apply_rho()"]
    Output["predictions<br/>(batch_size, output_size)"]
    
    Input --> PhiApp
    PhiApp --> RhoApp
    RhoApp --> Output
```

#### `_forward_spot_subspot(x)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:167-172]()

Processes spot features plus 9 mini-tiles (3×3 grid) within the spot.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["x = [x_spot, x_subspot]"]
    PhiSpot["_apply_phi(x_spot)<br/>operation=NONE"]
    PhiSub["_apply_phi(x_subspot)<br/>operation=agg_neighbors"]
    Concat["torch.cat()"]
    RhoApp["_apply_rho()"]
    Output["predictions"]
    
    Input --> PhiSpot
    Input --> PhiSub
    PhiSpot --> Concat
    PhiSub --> Concat
    Concat --> RhoApp
    RhoApp --> Output
```

#### `_forward_spot_neighbors(x)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:174-179]()

Processes spot features plus neighboring spots' features.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["x = [x_spot, x_neighbors]"]
    PhiSpot["_apply_phi(x_spot)<br/>operation=NONE"]
    PhiNeigh["_apply_phi(x_neighbors)<br/>operation=agg_neighbors"]
    Concat["torch.cat()"]
    RhoApp["_apply_rho()"]
    Output["predictions"]
    
    Input --> PhiSpot
    Input --> PhiNeigh
    PhiSpot --> Concat
    PhiNeigh --> Concat
    Concat --> RhoApp
    RhoApp --> Output
```

#### `_forward_spot_subspot_neighbors(x)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:181-187]()

Processes spot features, mini-tiles, and neighboring spots (full spatial context).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["x = [x_spot, x_subspot, x_neighbors]"]
    PhiSpot["_apply_phi(x_spot)<br/>operation=NONE"]
    PhiSub["_apply_phi(x_subspot)<br/>operation=agg_neighbors"]
    PhiNeigh["_apply_phi(x_neighbors)<br/>operation=agg_neighbors"]
    Concat["torch.cat()"]
    RhoApp["_apply_rho()"]
    Output["predictions"]
    
    Input --> PhiSpot
    Input --> PhiSub
    Input --> PhiNeigh
    PhiSpot --> Concat
    PhiSub --> Concat
    PhiNeigh --> Concat
    Concat --> RhoApp
    RhoApp --> Output
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:163-187](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:54-57]()

### Training Lifecycle Methods

The following methods manage the training and validation loop:

#### `training_step(batch, batch_idx)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:148-149]()

Called by Lightning for each training batch. Delegates to `loop_step()` with `stage="train"`.

#### `validation_step(batch, batch_idx)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:151-152]()

Called by Lightning for each validation batch. Delegates to `loop_step()` with `stage="val"`.

#### `loop_step(batch, stage)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:128-146]()

Core training/validation logic:
1. Unpacks batch into features `X` and labels `y`
2. Converts to float tensors
3. Performs forward pass: `y_hat = self(X)`
4. Computes loss: `loss = self.loss_func(y_hat, y)`
5. Logs loss and appends to `training_loss` or `validation_loss` lists

#### `configure_optimizers()`
Returns AdamW optimizer configured with `lr` and `weight_decay` parameters.

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:128-152](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:144-218]()

### Core Processing Methods

#### `_apply_phi(x, phi_modules, operation)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:189-208]()

Applies ensemble of Phi layers to input features:

1. Reshapes input to `(batch_size * sample_size, input_size)`
2. Applies all Phi modules in parallel: `[phi(x) for phi in phi_modules]`
3. Takes median across ensemble: `torch.median(..., dim=1)`
4. Reshapes back to `(batch_size, sample_size, phi2rho_size)`
5. Applies aggregation operation:
   - `Operation.SUM`: sums across sample dimension
   - `Operation.MEAN`: averages across sample dimension
   - `Operation.MAX`: takes maximum across sample dimension
   - `Operation.NONE`: flattens to `(batch_size, sample_size * phi2rho_size)`

#### `_apply_rho(x_phi)`
**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:210-213]()

Applies ensemble of Rho layers to Phi outputs:

1. Applies all Rho modules in parallel: `[rho(x_phi) for rho in self.rho]`
2. Takes mean across ensemble: `torch.mean(..., dim=1)`
3. Returns final predictions: `(batch_size, output_size)`

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:189-213](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-214]()

---

## DeepSpotDataLoader Class

The `DeepSpotDataLoader` is a PyTorch `Dataset` subclass for loading and preprocessing spot-level data.

**Location:** [deepspot/spot/dataloader.py]()

### Key Responsibilities

1. **Data Loading**: Loads gene expression matrices and image feature embeddings
2. **Spatial Processing**: Applies upsampling, smoothing, and normalization
3. **Neighbor Computation**: Identifies neighboring spots based on spatial coordinates
4. **Batching**: Returns batches of features and labels for training/validation

For detailed documentation of parameters and methods, see [DeepSpotDataLoader](#4.4).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282]() (by analogy with DeepCellDataLoader)

## Loss Functions

The `deepspot.spot.loss` module provides various loss functions for training:

### Available Loss Functions

| Function Name | Location | Description |
|---------------|----------|-------------|
| `loss_mse_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py:19-21]() | Mean Squared Error |
| `loss_pearson_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Negative Pearson correlation |
| `loss_cosine_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Cosine similarity loss |
| `loss_l1_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | L1 (MAE) loss |
| `loss_huber_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Huber loss (smooth L1) |
| `loss_poisson_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Poisson negative log-likelihood |
| `loss_mse_pearson_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Combined MSE + Pearson |
| `loss_mse_cosine_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Combined MSE + cosine |
| `loss_l1_cosine_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Combined L1 + cosine |
| `loss_huber_cosine_function` | [deepspot/spot/loss.py]() | Combined Huber + cosine |

### Loss Function Selection

Loss functions are selected by passing the appropriate string to `DeepSpot.__init__`:

```python
model = DeepSpot(
    input_size=1024,
    output_size=500,
    loss_func="mse_pearson"  # Uses combined MSE + Pearson loss
)
```

The mapping from string to function occurs in the `__init__` method via conditional logic similar to [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]().

For detailed discussion of when to use each loss function, see [Loss Functions](#5.4).

**Sources:** [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:93-100](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]()

## Phi and Rho Neural Layers

### Phi Layer

**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:31-41]()

The `Phi` class is a neural network module for feature transformation:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Input<br/>(batch, input_size)"]
    Linear["nn.Linear<br/>(input_size → output_size)"]
    Dropout["nn.Dropout(p)"]
    ReLU["nn.ReLU(inplace=True)"]
    Output["Output<br/>(batch, output_size)"]
    
    Input --> Linear
    Linear --> Dropout
    Dropout --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Output
```

**Figure 3: Phi Layer Architecture**

**Constructor Parameters:**
- `input_size` (int): Input feature dimension
- `output_size` (int): Output feature dimension (typically `phi2rho_size`)
- `p` (float): Dropout probability (default 0.0)

Multiple Phi modules are instantiated as an ensemble (default 10 modules), and their outputs are aggregated via median operation.

### Rho Layer

**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:44-55]()

The `Rho` class is a neural network module for final prediction:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Input<br/>(batch, input_size)"]
    Dropout1["nn.Dropout(p)"]
    ReLU["nn.ReLU(inplace=True)"]
    Linear["nn.Linear<br/>(input_size → output_size)"]
    Dropout2["nn.Dropout(0.1)"]
    Output["Output<br/>(batch, output_size)"]
    
    Input --> Dropout1
    Dropout1 --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Linear
    Linear --> Dropout2
    Dropout2 --> Output
```

**Figure 4: Rho Layer Architecture**

**Constructor Parameters:**
- `input_size` (int): Input feature dimension (typically `phi2rho_size * phi_multiplier`)
- `output_size` (int): Output dimension (number of genes)
- `p` (float): Dropout probability for first dropout layer (default 0.0)

Multiple Rho modules are instantiated as an ensemble (default 10 modules), and their outputs are aggregated via mean operation.

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:31-55](), [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:74-82](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:36-60]()

---

## Ensemble Architecture

The following diagram illustrates how Phi and Rho ensembles combine:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        Input["Input Features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phi Ensemble (n=10)"
        Phi1["Phi Module 1"]
        Phi2["Phi Module 2"]
        PhiDots["..."]
        Phi10["Phi Module 10"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phi Aggregation"
        MedianPhi["torch.median()<br/>across ensemble"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rho Ensemble (n=10)"
        Rho1["Rho Module 1"]
        Rho2["Rho Module 2"]
        RhoDots["..."]
        Rho10["Rho Module 10"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rho Aggregation"
        MeanRho["torch.mean()<br/>across ensemble"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Predictions["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    end
    
    Input --> Phi1
    Input --> Phi2
    Input --> PhiDots
    Input --> Phi10
    
    Phi1 --> MedianPhi
    Phi2 --> MedianPhi
    PhiDots --> MedianPhi
    Phi10 --> MedianPhi
    
    MedianPhi --> Rho1
    MedianPhi --> Rho2
    MedianPhi --> RhoDots
    MedianPhi --> Rho10
    
    Rho1 --> MeanRho
    Rho2 --> MeanRho
    RhoDots --> MeanRho
    Rho10 --> MeanRho
    
    MeanRho --> Predictions
```

**Figure 5: Complete Phi-Rho Ensemble Pipeline**

**Key Design Choices:**
- **Phi uses median aggregation**: More robust to outliers in ensemble predictions
- **Rho uses mean aggregation**: Smoother final predictions by averaging
- **Default ensemble size of 10**: Balances model capacity with computational cost

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-214](), [deepspot/spot/model.py:189-213]()

---

## Usage Patterns

### Basic Instantiation

```python
from deepspot.spot.model import DeepSpot

# Create model for 500 genes using UNI features (1024-dim)
model = DeepSpot(
    input_size=1024,
    output_size=500,
    loss_func="mse_pearson",
    lr=1e-4,
    spot_context="spot_subspot_neighbors"
)
```

### Training with Lightning

```python
import lightning as L
from deepspot.spot.dataloader import DeepSpotDataLoader

# Create data loaders
train_loader = DeepSpotDataLoader(...)
val_loader = DeepSpotDataLoader(...)

# Train with Lightning Trainer
trainer = L.Trainer(max_epochs=100, accelerator="gpu")
trainer.fit(model, train_loader, val_loader)
```

### Inference

```python
# Load trained model
model = DeepSpot.load_from_checkpoint("path/to/checkpoint.ckpt")
model.eval()

# Make predictions
with torch.no_grad():
    predictions = model(spot_features)
```

For complete workflow examples, see [Visium Training](#7.1.2) and [Visium Inference](#7.1.3).

**Sources:** [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282]()

---

## Key Implementation Details

### Phi Multiplier Calculation

The `_get_phi_multiplier()` method determines the size of the feature vector passed to Rho layers based on spot context:

| Spot Context | Phi Multiplier | Rho Input Size |
|--------------|----------------|----------------|
| `"spot"` | 1 | `phi2rho_size` |
| `"spot_subspot"` | 2 | `phi2rho_size * 2` |
| `"spot_neighbors"` | 2 | `phi2rho_size * 2` |
| `"spot_subspot_neighbors"` | 3 | `phi2rho_size * 3` |

**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-117]()

### Forward Function Dispatch

The `_get_forward_function()` method maps spot context strings to forward methods:

**Location:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:119-126]()

This mapping is established during `__init__` and stored as `self._forward_fn`, which is called by the main `forward()` method.

**Sources:** [deepspot/spot/model.py:110-126](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:130-142]()

---

## Comparison with DeepCell

The following table summarizes key differences between `deepspot.spot` and `deepspot.cell`:

| Aspect | DeepSpot (Spot) | DeepCell (Cell) |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Resolution** | ~55μm (Visium spots) | ~20μm (single cells) |
| **Context Modes** | 4 modes: spot, spot_subspot, spot_neighbors, spot_subspot_neighbors | 2 modes: cell, cell_neighbors |
| **Mini-tiles** | Supports 3×3 sub-tiles per spot | No sub-tiles (cells too small) |
| **Typical Gene Count** | 300-800 highly variable genes | 500 highly variable genes |
| **Module Location** | [deepspot/spot/model.py]() | [deepspot/cell/model.py]() |

Both models share the same Phi-Rho ensemble architecture and loss function options, differing primarily in spatial context handling.

**Sources:** [.codeboarding/DeepSpot Models.md:1-113](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:1-282]()

---

# Page: deepspot.utils

# deepspot.utils

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot/utils/utils.py](deepspot/utils/utils.py)
- [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py](deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py)
- [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py](deepspot/utils/utils_image.py)

</details>



The `deepspot.utils` module provides utility functions for data loading, image processing, spatial transcriptomics preprocessing, and model training/inference. This module is divided into three submodules:

- `deepspot.utils.utils_dataloader` - Functions for loading gene expression data, computing spatial neighbors, upsampling, and smoothing
- `deepspot.utils.utils_image` - Functions for loading foundation models, preprocessing images, extracting tiles, and running inference from image paths
- `deepspot.utils.utils` - General utilities for model fine-tuning, inference, seeding, and visualization

For model-specific data loaders, see [deepspot.cell](#9.1) and [deepspot.spot](#9.2). For high-level workflow documentation, see [Visium Spot Workflow](#7.1) and [Xenium Cell Workflow](#7.2).

---

## deepspot.utils.utils_dataloader

This module provides functions for loading spatial transcriptomics data, performing spatial upsampling and smoothing, computing spatial neighbors, and preprocessing gene expression counts.

### load_data

```python
def load_data(
    samples,
    out_folder,
    feature_model=None,
    cell_diameter=None,
    load_image_features=True,
    factor=10000,
    raw_counts=False
)
```

Loads gene expression data and optionally image features from pickle files organized by sample.

**Parameters:**
- `samples` (list of str): List of sample identifiers
- `out_folder` (str): Base directory containing `data/inputX/` and `data/image_features/` subdirectories
- `feature_model` (str, optional): Name of the foundation model used for feature extraction (e.g., "uni", "hoptimus0", "phikon")
- `cell_diameter` (int, optional): Diameter in pixels used during feature extraction (used for cell-level data)
- `load_image_features` (bool): Whether to load pre-extracted image features
- `factor` (int): Normalization factor for log1p normalization (default: 10000)
- `raw_counts` (bool): If True, skip log1p normalization

**Returns:**
- `dict`: Dictionary with keys:
  - `"y"` (np.ndarray): Gene expression matrix (log-normalized unless `raw_counts=True`)
  - `"X"` (pd.DataFrame): Image features (if `load_image_features=True`)
  - `"barcode"` (np.ndarray): Cell/spot barcodes

**Expected Directory Structure:**
```
out_folder/
├── data/
│   ├── inputX/
│   │   ├── sample1.pkl
│   │   └── sample2.pkl
│   └── image_features/
│       ├── uni/
│       │   ├── sample1.pkl
│       │   └── sample2.pkl
│       └── hoptimus0_40/
│           ├── sample1.pkl
│           └── sample2.pkl
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:132-174]()

---

### spatial_upsample_and_smooth

```python
def spatial_upsample_and_smooth(
    counts,
    obs,
    barcode,
    resolution,
    smooth_n=0,
    augmentation="default"
)
```

Performs spatial upsampling through clustering-based resampling and optionally smooths gene expression using k-nearest neighbors.

**Parameters:**
- `counts` (np.ndarray): Gene expression matrix (spots/cells × genes)
- `obs` (pd.DataFrame): Observation metadata with spatial coordinates
- `barcode` (np.ndarray): Cell/spot identifiers formatted as `prefix_sampleID_suffix`
- `resolution` (float): Leiden clustering resolution; if 0, no upsampling is performed
- `smooth_n` (int): Number of nearest neighbors for smoothing; if 0, no smoothing
- `augmentation` (str): Clustering method - "default" (PCA + Leiden) or "aestetik" (AESTETIK spatial clustering)

**Returns:**
- `tuple`:
  - `resampled_barcodes` (np.ndarray): Upsampled barcode list
  - `transcriptomics_smooth` (np.ndarray): Smoothed expression matrix

**Workflow:**
1. Groups data by sample (extracted from barcode format)
2. Runs PCA and Leiden clustering at specified resolution
3. Balances cluster sizes by resampling from each cluster
4. Optionally smooths expression by averaging k-nearest neighbors in latent space

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:65-98]()

---

### compute_neighbors

```python
def compute_neighbors(row, coordinates, radius=1)
```

Finds spatial neighbors within a square radius for a given spot/cell.

**Parameters:**
- `row` (pd.Series): Row from coordinates DataFrame containing `x_array`, `y_array`, `sampleID`, and `barcode`
- `coordinates` (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with columns `x_array`, `y_array`, `sampleID`, `barcode` for all spots/cells
- `radius` (int): Square radius for neighbor search (default: 1, which creates a 3×3 grid)

**Returns:**
- `str`: Neighbor barcodes joined by "___" separator (excludes the query cell/spot itself)

**Query Logic:**
The function constructs a pandas query that finds neighbors where:
- `(x_array - radius) <= query_x <= (x_array + radius)`
- `(y_array - radius) <= query_y <= (y_array + radius)`
- Same `sampleID` but different `barcode`

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:112-121]()

---

### log1p_normalization

```python
def log1p_normalization(arr, factor=10000, eps=1e-12)
```

Applies standard single-cell RNA-seq normalization: library size normalization followed by log1p transformation.

**Parameters:**
- `arr` (np.ndarray): Raw count matrix (spots/cells × genes)
- `factor` (int): Scaling factor (default: 10000)
- `eps` (float): Small constant to avoid division by zero

**Returns:**
- `np.ndarray`: Normalized matrix

**Formula:**
```
log1p((arr / (sum(arr, axis=1) + eps)) * factor)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py:128-129]()

---

### Supporting Functions

| Function | Purpose | Source |
|----------|---------|--------|
| `get_balanced_index()` | Randomly samples cells/spots from each cluster to balance sizes | [utils_dataloader.py:20-26]() |
| `run_default()` | Runs PCA + Leiden clustering | [utils_dataloader.py:29-37]() |
| `run_aestetik()` | Runs AESTETIK spatial clustering | [utils_dataloader.py:40-62]() |
| `add_zero_padding()` | Pads arrays with zeros to desired size | [utils_dataloader.py:101-109]() |
| `load_multiple_pickles()` | Loads and concatenates multiple pickle files | [utils_dataloader.py:124-125]() |

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_dataloader.py]()

### get_morphology_model_and_preprocess

```python
def get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(model_name, device, model_path=None)
```

Loads a pathology foundation model or classical CNN with appropriate preprocessing transforms.

**Parameters:**
- `model_name` (str): Model identifier - "uni", "hoptimus0", "phikon", "phikonv2", "inception", "resnet50", "densenet121"
- `device` (torch.device): Device for model loading
- `model_path` (str, optional): Path to model weights (required for "uni", "hoptimus0", "phikon", "phikonv2")

**Returns:**
- `tuple`:
  - `morphology_model` (torch.nn.Module): Loaded model in eval mode
  - `preprocess` (callable): Preprocessing function for input images
  - `feature_dim` (int): Output feature dimension

**Model Details:**

| Model Name | Architecture | Feature Dim | Normalization Mean | Normalization Std |
|------------|--------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| uni | ViT-Large-16-224 | 1024 | (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) | (0.229, 0.224, 0.225) |
| hoptimus0 | ViT-Giant-14-DINOv2 | 1536 | (0.707, 0.579, 0.704) | (0.212, 0.230, 0.178) |
| phikon | ViT-Base | 768 | HuggingFace AutoProcessor | HuggingFace AutoProcessor |
| phikonv2 | ViT-Base | 1024 | HuggingFace AutoProcessor | HuggingFace AutoProcessor |
| inception | Inception v3 | 2048 | ImageNet default | ImageNet default |
| resnet50 | ResNet-50 | 2048 | ImageNet default | ImageNet default |
| densenet121 | DenseNet-121 | 1024 | ImageNet default | ImageNet default |

**Usage Example:**
```python
model, preprocess, feature_dim = get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(
    model_name="uni",
    device=torch.device("cuda"),
    model_path="/path/to/uni_weights.pth"
)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:36-177]()

### crop_tile

```python
def crop_tile(image, x_pixel, y_pixel, cell_diameter)
```

Extracts a square tile centered at specified pixel coordinates from a pyvips image.

**Parameters:**
- `image` (pyvips.Image): Opened whole-slide image
- `x_pixel` (int): X-coordinate of tile center
- `y_pixel` (int): Y-coordinate of tile center
- `cell_diameter` (int): Side length of square tile in pixels

**Returns:**
- `np.ndarray`: RGB image tile of shape `(cell_diameter, cell_diameter, 3)`

**Implementation Details:**
- Converts center coordinates to top-left corner: `x = x_pixel - (cell_diameter // 2)`
- Uses pyvips crop for memory-efficient extraction
- Truncates to 3 channels (RGB) if image has more

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:190-198]()

---

### compute_mini_tiles

```python
def compute_mini_tiles(image, n_tiles, super_resolution_mode=False)
```

Splits a square image into n×n smaller tiles for sub-spot analysis.

**Parameters:**
- `image` (np.ndarray): Square image of shape `(D, D, 3)`
- `n_tiles` (int): Total number of tiles (must be perfect square, typically 9 for 3×3 grid)
- `super_resolution_mode` (bool): If True, extracts only the center tile

**Returns:**
- `list` of `np.ndarray`: List of sub-tile images

**Typical Usage:**
- For Visium spots: `n_tiles=9` creates a 3×3 grid, capturing sub-spot heterogeneity
- For super-resolution: extracts center region only

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:201-234]()

### Inference from Image Paths

These functions provide end-to-end inference pipelines that load images, extract features on-the-fly, and predict gene expression without requiring pre-extracted features.

### predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path

```python
def predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path(
    image_path,
    adata,
    spot_diameter,
    n_mini_tiles,
    preprocess,
    morphology_model,
    model_expression,
    device,
    super_resolution=False,
    neighbor_radius=1
)
```

Performs spot-level spatial transcriptomics prediction directly from an H&E image path.

**Parameters:**
- `image_path` (str): Path to whole-slide image
- `adata` (AnnData): AnnData object with `.obs` containing `x_pixel`, `y_pixel`, `barcode`, `sampleID` columns
- `spot_diameter` (int): Spot diameter in pixels
- `n_mini_tiles` (int): Number of sub-tiles (typically 9)
- `preprocess` (callable): Preprocessing function from `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()`
- `morphology_model` (torch.nn.Module): Foundation model for feature extraction
- `model_expression` (DeepSpot): Trained DeepSpot model
- `device` (torch.device): Computation device
- `super_resolution` (bool): If True, uses only center sub-tile
- `neighbor_radius` (int): Radius for neighbor search (default: 1)

**Returns:**
- `np.ndarray`: Predicted gene expression matrix of shape `(n_spots, n_genes)`

**Workflow:**
1. Opens image with pyvips for memory efficiency
2. For each spot in `adata.obs`:
   - Extracts main spot tile at `(x_pixel, y_pixel)`
   - Computes `n_mini_tiles` sub-tiles
   - Finds neighbor spots within `neighbor_radius`
   - Extracts tiles for each neighbor
3. Applies preprocessing to all tiles
4. Passes through `morphology_model` to extract features
5. Feeds features to `model_expression` for gene prediction
6. Inverse-transforms predictions to original scale

**Performance Optimizations:**
- Uses `torch.autocast` for mixed precision (FP16)
- Uses `torch.inference_mode()` for faster inference
- Processes one spot at a time to manage memory

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:241-292]()

---

### predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path

```python
def predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path(
    image_path,
    adata,
    cell_diameter,
    radius_neighbors,
    preprocess,
    morphology_model,
    model_expression,
    device
)
```

Performs cell-level spatial transcriptomics prediction directly from an H&E image path.

**Parameters:**
- `image_path` (str): Path to whole-slide image
- `adata` (AnnData): AnnData object with `.obs` containing `x_pixel`, `y_pixel`, `barcode` columns
- `cell_diameter` (int): Cell diameter in pixels
- `radius_neighbors` (float): Radius in pixels for neighbor search (e.g., 45 for Xenium)
- `preprocess` (callable): Preprocessing function from `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()`
- `morphology_model` (torch.nn.Module): Foundation model for feature extraction
- `model_expression` (DeepCell): Trained DeepCell model
- `device` (torch.device): Computation device

**Returns:**
- `np.ndarray`: Predicted gene expression matrix of shape `(n_cells, n_genes)`

**Workflow:**
1. Computes neighbors using `sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors` with radius search
2. Stores neighbor lists in `adata.obs["neighbors"]` as "___"-separated strings
3. For each cell:
   - Extracts main cell tile
   - Extracts tiles for all neighbors within radius
   - Applies preprocessing and feature extraction
   - Predicts gene expression
4. Returns predictions in original scale

**Differences from Spot Prediction:**
- No sub-tile computation (cells are smaller than spots)
- Uses radius-based neighbor search instead of grid-based
- Typically more neighbors per cell (e.g., 45-pixel radius for Xenium)

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:295-356]()

---

### Inference Pipeline Comparison

| Aspect | Spot Inference | Cell Inference |
|--------|---------------|----------------|
| Function | `predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()` | `predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()` |
| Model Type | DeepSpot | DeepCell |
| Sub-tiles | Yes (3×3 grid = 9 tiles) | No |
| Neighbor Search | Grid-based with radius | Distance-based with radius |
| Typical Neighbor Count | ~8 (for radius=1) | ~45 (for radius=45 pixels) |
| Input Components | [spot_tile, sub_tiles, neighbor_tiles] | [cell_tile, neighbor_tiles] |

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils_image.py:241-356]()

---

## deepspot.utils.utils

This module provides general utilities for model training, inference, reproducibility, and visualization.

### model_fine_tune

```python
def model_fine_tune(
    model,
    dataloader,
    rho=False,
    gene_expression=True,
    max_epochs=10
)
```

Fine-tunes specific layers of a pre-trained model while keeping other layers frozen.

**Parameters:**
- `model` (DeepSpot or DeepCell): Pre-trained model to fine-tune
- `dataloader` (DataLoader): Training data loader
- `rho` (bool): If True, unfreeze and train the `rho` ensemble layers
- `gene_expression` (bool): If True, unfreeze and train the final `gene_expression` layer
- `max_epochs` (int): Number of training epochs

**Workflow:**
1. Freezes all model parameters
2. Selectively unfreezes specified layers (`rho`, `gene_expression`)
3. Creates AdamW optimizer with only trainable parameters
4. Sets model to eval mode, but unfrozen layers to train mode
5. Trains using PyTorch Lightning trainer

**Typical Usage:**
Fine-tune only the final prediction layer when adapting to a new dataset:
```python
model_fine_tune(model, train_loader, rho=False, gene_expression=True, max_epochs=10)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-48]()

---

### run_inference_from_dataloader

```python
def run_inference_from_dataloader(model, dataloader, device)
```

Runs batch inference on a dataset using a data loader.

**Parameters:**
- `model` (torch.nn.Module): Trained model
- `dataloader` (DataLoader): Data loader yielding batches
- `device` (torch.device): Device for computation

**Returns:**
- `np.ndarray`: Concatenated predictions from all batches

**Workflow:**
1. Moves model to specified device and sets to eval mode
2. Iterates through batches with `torch.no_grad()`
3. Handles both single-tensor and list-of-tensors inputs
4. Moves predictions to CPU and converts to NumPy
5. Concatenates all batch predictions

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:51-69]()

---

### fix_seed

```python
def fix_seed(seed)
```

Sets random seeds for all libraries to ensure reproducible results.

**Parameters:**
- `seed` (int): Random seed value

**Libraries Configured:**
- Python's built-in `random` module
- NumPy random generator
- PyTorch CPU and CUDA random generators
- CuDNN deterministic mode
- CUBLAS workspace configuration

**Environment Variables Set:**
- `PYTHONHASHSEED`: Python hash randomization
- `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`: CUDA deterministic algorithms

**Usage:**
```python
fix_seed(42)  # Ensures reproducible training and inference
```

**Note:** Enabling deterministic mode may impact performance. See [Reproducibility & Seeding](#10.3) for details.

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:89-100]()

---

### plot_loss_values

```python
def plot_loss_values(train_losses, val_losses=None)
```

Visualizes training and optionally validation loss curves.

**Parameters:**
- `train_losses` (list or np.ndarray): Training loss values per iteration
- `val_losses` (list or np.ndarray, optional): Validation loss values (recorded less frequently than training)

**Plot Details:**
- X-axis: Iteration/epoch
- Y-axis: Loss value
- Blue line: Training loss
- Red line: Validation loss (if provided)
- Automatically aligns validation points based on frequency difference

**Sources:** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:72-86]()

```mermaid
graph TB

    GetModel --> Features
    CropTiles --> ComputeSub
    ComputeSub --> ExtractFeat
    ExtractFeat --> Features
    
    NewWSI --> PredictFunc
    PredictFunc --> Predictions
    Predictions --> InverseTransform
    InverseTransform --> FinalPred
```

## Model Fine-tuning

DeepSpot and DeepCell models can be fine-tuned on new datasets by selectively unfreezing specific layers while keeping pretrained weights frozen in other parts of the network. This approach is particularly useful when adapting models trained on one tissue type to another, or when working with limited training data.

### Fine-tuning Architecture

The `model_fine_tune` function [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-48]() implements layer-selective fine-tuning by controlling gradient flow through the model:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Fine-tuning Process"
        Model["Pretrained Model<br/>(DeepCell or DeepSpot)"]
        Freeze["Freeze All Layers<br/>param.requires_grad = False"]
        Unfreeze["Selective Unfreezing"]
        Optimizer["AdamW Optimizer<br/>(trainable params only)"]
        Train["Lightning Trainer<br/>(max_epochs)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Layer Selection"
        Rho["Rho Layers<br/>model.rho<br/>(if rho=True)"]
        GeneExpr["Gene Expression Layer<br/>model.gene_expression<br/>(if gene_expression=True)"]
    end
    
    Model --> Freeze
    Freeze --> Unfreeze
    Unfreeze --> Rho
    Unfreeze --> GeneExpr
    Rho --> Optimizer
    GeneExpr --> Optimizer
    Optimizer --> Train
    
    style Model fill:#e1f5ff
    style Unfreeze fill:#fff4e1
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-48]()

### Function Signature

```python
model_fine_tune(model, dataloader, rho=False, gene_expression=True, max_epochs=10)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `model` | `L.LightningModule` | Required | Pretrained DeepCell or DeepSpot model |
| `dataloader` | `DataLoader` | Required | Fine-tuning dataset loader |
| `rho` | `bool` | `False` | Unfreeze Rho ensemble layers for training |
| `gene_expression` | `bool` | `True` | Unfreeze gene expression prediction layer |
| `max_epochs` | `int` | `10` | Number of fine-tuning epochs |

### Implementation Details

The fine-tuning process operates in four stages:

1. **Global Freeze** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:22-23](): All model parameters are frozen by setting `requires_grad=False`

2. **Selective Unfreeze** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:25-32](): Target layers are unfrozen based on flags:
   - `rho=True`: Unfreezes `model.rho` (the Rho ensemble modules)
   - `gene_expression=True`: Unfreezes `model.gene_expression` layer (if present)

3. **Optimizer Reconfiguration** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:35-38](): A new AdamW optimizer is created with filtered parameters that only includes trainable layers

4. **Targeted Training** [deepspot/utils/utils.py:39-48](): Model is set to eval mode globally, but unfrozen layers are explicitly set to train mode before fitting

### Usage Pattern

```python
# Load pretrained model
from deepspot.cell.model import DeepCell
model = DeepCell.load_from_checkpoint("pretrained_weights.ckpt")

# Prepare fine-tuning dataloader
from deepspot.cell.dataloader import DeepCellDataLoader
fine_tune_loader = DeepCellDataLoader(...)

# Fine-tune only the Rho layers
from deepspot.utils.utils import model_fine_tune
model_fine_tune(
    model=model,
    dataloader=fine_tune_loader,
    rho=True,
    gene_expression=False,
    max_epochs=5
)
```

### Recommended Fine-tuning Strategies

| Scenario | Rho Setting | Gene Expression Setting | Rationale |
|----------|-------------|------------------------|-----------|
| New tissue type, same genes | `True` | `True` | Adapt aggregation and final prediction |
| Similar tissue, different staining | `False` | `True` | Only adjust final gene mapping |
| Limited training data | `True` | `False` | Fine-tune aggregation, preserve gene weights |
| Domain adaptation | `True` | `True` | Full fine-tuning of prediction layers |

**Sources**: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-48]()

---

## Custom Loss Functions

DeepSpot supports multiple loss functions for training, each optimizing different aspects of gene expression prediction. Custom loss functions can be implemented by following the established patterns in the codebase.

### Loss Function Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Loss Function Selection"
        Init["Model Initialization<br/>loss_func parameter"]
        Map["Loss Function Mapping"]
        Assign["self.loss_func assignment"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Available Loss Functions"
        MSE["loss_mse_function<br/>Mean Squared Error"]
        Pearson["loss_pearson_function<br/>Pearson Correlation"]
        Cosine["loss_cosine_function<br/>Cosine Similarity"]
        L1["loss_l1_function<br/>L1 Loss"]
        Huber["loss_huber_function<br/>Huber Loss"]
        Poisson["loss_poisson_function<br/>Poisson Loss"]
        Combined1["loss_mse_pearson_function<br/>MSE + Pearson"]
        Combined2["loss_mse_cosine_function<br/>MSE + Cosine"]
        Combined3["loss_l1_cosine_function<br/>L1 + Cosine"]
        Combined4["loss_huber_cosine_function<br/>Huber + Cosine"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Loop"
        Forward["Model Forward Pass"]
        Loss["Loss Computation<br/>self.loss_func(y_hat, y)"]
        Backward["Backpropagation"]
    end
    
    Init --> Map
    Map --> MSE
    Map --> Pearson
    Map --> Cosine
    Map --> L1
    Map --> Huber
    Map --> Poisson
    Map --> Combined1
    Map --> Combined2
    Map --> Combined3
    Map --> Combined4
    
    MSE --> Assign
    Pearson --> Assign
    Cosine --> Assign
    L1 --> Assign
    Huber --> Assign
    Poisson --> Assign
    Combined1 --> Assign
    Combined2 --> Assign
    Combined3 --> Assign
    Combined4 --> Assign
    
    Assign --> Loss
    Forward --> Loss
    Loss --> Backward
    
    style Map fill:#fff4e1
    style Loss fill:#ffe1f5
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107](), [deepspot/cell/loss.py]()

### Loss Function Selection in DeepCell

The loss function is specified during model initialization [deepspot/cell/model.py:64-82]() and mapped to the corresponding implementation [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]():

| String Identifier | Function Name | Use Case |
|-------------------|---------------|----------|
| `"mse"` | `loss_mse_function` | Standard regression, penalizes large errors quadratically |
| `"cos"` | `loss_cosine_function` | Pattern matching, ignores magnitude differences |
| `"l1"` | `loss_l1_function` | Robust to outliers, penalizes errors linearly |
| `"huber"` | `loss_huber_function` | Hybrid approach, quadratic near zero, linear for large errors |
| `"mse_cos"` | `loss_mse_cosine_function` | Combined magnitude and pattern matching |
| `"l1_cos"` | `loss_l1_cosine_function` | Outlier-robust pattern matching |
| `"huber_cos"` | `loss_huber_cosine_function` | Robust hybrid with pattern matching |
| `"pearson"` | `loss_pearson_function` | Correlation-based, scale-invariant |
| `"mse_pearson"` | `loss_mse_pearson_function` | Combined magnitude and correlation |
| `"poisson"` | `loss_poisson_function` | Count data modeling, assumes Poisson distribution |

### Implementing Custom Loss Functions

To implement a custom loss function:

1. **Create Loss Function**: Define a function that accepts `y_hat` (predictions) and `y` (ground truth) tensors and returns a scalar loss

2. **Import in Model**: Add the import statement to [deepspot/cell/model.py:13-24]() or [deepspot/spot/model.py]()

3. **Add to Mapping**: Extend the conditional mapping in model initialization [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]()

4. **Specify During Training**: Pass the new identifier string when instantiating the model

Example custom loss function structure:

```python
def loss_custom_function(y_hat: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Custom loss function implementation.
    
    Args:
        y_hat: Predicted gene expression [batch_size, n_genes]
        y: Ground truth gene expression [batch_size, n_genes]
    
    Returns:
        Scalar loss value
    """
    # Implementation here
    loss = custom_computation(y_hat, y)
    return loss
```

### Loss Function Combination Patterns

Combined loss functions are implemented as weighted sums of individual components. For example, `loss_mse_cosine_function` combines:
- MSE component: Penalizes magnitude errors
- Cosine component: Penalizes pattern mismatches

This dual optimization encourages predictions that are both accurate in absolute value and maintain correct gene expression patterns.

**Sources**: [deepspot/cell/model.py:13-24](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:88-107]()

---

## Reproducibility & Seeding

Ensuring reproducible results is critical for scientific validation and debugging. DeepSpot implements comprehensive seeding through the `fix_seed` function.

### Reproducibility Components

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "fix_seed Function"
        Input["Random Seed<br/>(e.g., 2024)"]
        PythonHash["PYTHONHASHSEED<br/>environment variable"]
        PythonRandom["random.seed()"]
        NumPyRandom["np.random.seed()"]
        TorchCPU["torch.manual_seed()"]
        TorchGPU["torch.cuda.manual_seed_all()"]
        CuDNN["cudnn.deterministic = True<br/>cudnn.benchmark = False"]
        CUBLAS["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG<br/>environment variable"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Integration"
        ModelInit["DeepCell.__init__()<br/>DeepSpot.__init__()"]
        CallFixSeed["fix_seed(random_seed)"]
    end
    
    Input --> PythonHash
    Input --> PythonRandom
    Input --> NumPyRandom
    Input --> TorchCPU
    Input --> TorchGPU
    PythonHash --> CuDNN
    TorchGPU --> CuDNN
    CuDNN --> CUBLAS
    
    ModelInit --> CallFixSeed
    CallFixSeed --> Input
    
    style Input fill:#e1f5ff
    style CuDNN fill:#ffe1e1
    style CUBLAS fill:#ffe1e1
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:89-100](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:26](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:86]()

### Fix Seed Implementation

The `fix_seed` function [deepspot/utils/utils.py:89-100]() configures all random number generators to ensure deterministic behavior:

| Component | Configuration | Purpose |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| **Python Hash** | `PYTHONHASHSEED=str(seed)` | Deterministic hash-based operations |
| **Python Random** | `random.seed(seed)` | Standard library random module |
| **NumPy** | `np.random.seed(seed)` | NumPy array operations |
| **PyTorch CPU** | `torch.manual_seed(seed)` | CPU tensor operations |
| **PyTorch GPU (single)** | `torch.cuda.manual_seed(seed)` | Single GPU operations |
| **PyTorch GPU (multi)** | `torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)` | Multi-GPU operations |
| **cuDNN Determinism** | `cudnn.deterministic=True` | Disable non-deterministic algorithms |
| **cuDNN Benchmark** | `cudnn.benchmark=False` | Disable auto-tuning (non-deterministic) |
| **CUBLAS Workspace** | `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` | Deterministic CUBLAS operations |

### Automatic Seeding in Models

Models automatically call `fix_seed` during initialization [deepspot/cell/model.py:86]():

```python
def __init__(self, ..., random_seed: int = 2024, ...):
    super().__init__()
    self.save_hyperparameters()
    fix_seed(random_seed)
    # ... rest of initialization
```

The default seed is `2024`, but can be overridden during model instantiation.

### Reproducibility Best Practices

1. **Set Seed Before Training**: The seed is automatically set during model initialization
2. **Disable Workers**: For perfect reproducibility, set `num_workers=0` in DataLoader
3. **Single GPU**: Multi-GPU training may introduce non-determinism even with seeding
4. **Document Seeds**: Save the `random_seed` hyperparameter with model checkpoints
5. **Environment Variables**: Ensure `PYTHONHASHSEED` and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` are set before Python starts

### Performance Trade-offs

Enabling full determinism has performance implications:

| Setting | Impact | Severity |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `cudnn.deterministic=True` | Disables faster non-deterministic algorithms | Moderate (10-30% slower) |
| `cudnn.benchmark=False` | Prevents kernel auto-tuning | Minor (5-10% slower) |
| `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` | Uses deterministic workspace for CUBLAS | Minor (< 5% slower) |
| `num_workers=0` | Disables multi-process data loading | Severe (can be 2-5x slower) |

For production inference where reproducibility is less critical, consider disabling deterministic mode by not calling `fix_seed` or setting `cudnn.benchmark=True` manually.

**Sources**: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:89-100](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:86]()

---

## Performance Optimization

Optimizing training and inference performance involves careful configuration of batching, memory management, and hardware utilization.

### Training Performance Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Data Loading Stage"
        Disk["Preprocessed Features<br/>.npy files on disk"]
        Loader["DataLoader<br/>num_workers, batch_size"]
        Prefetch["Prefetching<br/>pin_memory=True"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Forward Stage"
        GPU["GPU Transfer"]
        PhiEnsemble["Phi Ensemble<br/>n=10 parallel modules<br/>median aggregation"]
        RhoEnsemble["Rho Ensemble<br/>n=10 parallel modules<br/>mean aggregation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optimization Stage"
        Loss["Loss Computation"]
        Backward["Backward Pass"]
        Optimizer["AdamW Optimizer<br/>weight_decay, lr"]
    end
    
    Disk --> Loader
    Loader --> Prefetch
    Prefetch --> GPU
    GPU --> PhiEnsemble
    PhiEnsemble --> RhoEnsemble
    RhoEnsemble --> Loss
    Loss --> Backward
    Backward --> Optimizer
    
    style Loader fill:#fff4e1
    style GPU fill:#ffe1e1
    style PhiEnsemble fill:#e1f5ff
```

**Sources**: [deepspot/cell/model.py:125-127](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:190-214]()

### Batch Size Configuration

Optimal batch size depends on GPU memory and model size:

| Model Type | Input Size | Typical Batch Size | GPU Memory |
|------------|------------|-------------------|------------|
| DeepCell (UNI) | 1024-dim | 32-64 | 8GB |
| DeepCell (Hoptimus0) | 1536-dim | 16-32 | 8GB |
| DeepSpot (neighbors) | Variable | 16-32 | 8GB |
| DeepSpot (subspot) | 9 × feature_dim | 8-16 | 8GB |

Larger batch sizes generally improve GPU utilization but require more memory. Monitor GPU memory usage with `nvidia-smi` during training.

### DataLoader Workers

The `num_workers` parameter in DataLoader controls multi-process data loading:

```python
dataloader = DataLoader(
    dataset,
    batch_size=32,
    num_workers=4,        # 4 parallel workers
    pin_memory=True,      # Enable for GPU training
    persistent_workers=True  # Keep workers alive between epochs
)
```

| Configuration | Use Case | Trade-off |
|---------------|----------|-----------|
| `num_workers=0` | Debugging, reproducibility | Slow data loading |
| `num_workers=2-4` | Small datasets, fast SSDs | Balanced |
| `num_workers=4-8` | Large datasets, slow disks | Maximum throughput, high CPU usage |
| `pin_memory=True` | GPU training | Faster CPU→GPU transfer, more memory |
| `persistent_workers=True` | Multi-epoch training | Faster epoch transitions, persistent memory |

### Memory Management Strategies

1. **Gradient Accumulation**: Simulate larger batch sizes with limited memory
   ```python
   accumulation_steps = 4
   for i, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
       loss = model.training_step(batch, i)
       loss = loss / accumulation_steps
       loss.backward()
       
       if (i + 1) % accumulation_steps == 0:
           optimizer.step()
           optimizer.zero_grad()
   ```

2. **Mixed Precision Training**: Use PyTorch Lightning's `precision` flag
   ```python
   trainer = L.Trainer(
       precision="16-mixed",  # or "bf16-mixed" for newer GPUs
       max_epochs=100
   )
   ```

3. **Gradient Checkpointing**: Trade computation for memory (not implemented in current version)

### Inference Optimization

The `run_inference_from_dataloader` function [deepspot/utils/utils.py:51-69]() provides efficient batch inference:

```python
from deepspot.utils.utils import run_inference_from_dataloader

# Efficient batch inference
predictions = run_inference_from_dataloader(
    model=model,
    dataloader=inference_loader,
    device='cuda'
)
```

Key optimizations:
- **Batch Processing**: Processes multiple samples simultaneously
- **No Gradient Computation**: Uses `torch.no_grad()` to disable gradient tracking
- **Device Management**: Handles CPU↔GPU transfers automatically
- **Progress Tracking**: Uses `tqdm` for progress visualization

### Ensemble Configuration

Models use ensemble architectures [deepspot/cell/model.py:118-127]() with configurable sizes:

| Parameter | Default | Range | Impact |
|-----------|---------|-------|--------|
| `n_ensemble` | 10 | 1-20 | Overall ensemble size (if not overridden) |
| `n_ensemble_phi` | `n_ensemble` | 1-20 | Number of Phi modules, improves feature robustness |
| `n_ensemble_rho` | `n_ensemble` | 1-20 | Number of Rho modules, improves prediction stability |

Reducing ensemble size decreases model parameters and speeds up training/inference:
- `n_ensemble=5`: ~50% faster, slightly lower accuracy
- `n_ensemble=10`: Default balance
- `n_ensemble=15`: ~50% slower, marginal accuracy improvement

### Hardware-Specific Optimizations

| GPU Type | Recommended Settings |
|----------|---------------------|
| **V100/A100** | `precision="16-mixed"`, `num_workers=8`, batch_size=64 |
| **RTX 3090/4090** | `precision="bf16-mixed"`, `num_workers=4`, batch_size=32 |
| **GTX 1080 Ti** | `precision=32`, `num_workers=2`, batch_size=16 |
| **CPU Only** | `num_workers=4-8`, batch_size=8, use smaller ensembles |

### Monitoring Performance

Use Lightning's built-in profiler to identify bottlenecks:

```python
from lightning.pytorch.profilers import SimpleProfiler

profiler = SimpleProfiler(filename="profile.txt")
trainer = L.Trainer(profiler=profiler)
trainer.fit(model, dataloader)
```

Key metrics to monitor:
- **Data loading time**: Should be < 10% of step time
- **GPU utilization**: Target 80-95% during training
- **Memory usage**: Leave 10-20% headroom to prevent OOM errors

**Sources**: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:51-69](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:118-127](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:216-218]()

---

# Page: Model Fine-tuning

# Model Fine-tuning

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot/cell/model.py](deepspot/cell/model.py)
- [deepspot/utils/utils.py](deepspot/utils/utils.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document describes how to fine-tune pre-trained DeepSpot and DeepCell models on new datasets using the `model_fine_tune` function. Fine-tuning allows you to adapt models trained on one dataset to perform better on a different but related dataset by selectively retraining specific layers while keeping others frozen. This approach leverages transfer learning to achieve better performance with less training time and data compared to training from scratch.

For information about training models from scratch, see [Visium Training](#7.1.2) and [Xenium Training](#7.2.2). For downloading and using pre-trained weights, see [Downloading Pre-trained Weights](#8.1).

---

## What is Fine-tuning?

Fine-tuning is a transfer learning technique where a pre-trained model is adapted to a new dataset by:

1. **Freezing** most model parameters to preserve learned features
2. **Unfreezing** specific layers (typically the final prediction layers) to allow adaptation
3. **Training** only the unfrozen layers on the new dataset with a smaller learning rate

In the DeepSpot architecture, fine-tuning is particularly useful when:
- You have a pre-trained model on one tissue type and want to adapt it to a different tissue
- Your new dataset has fewer samples than the original training set
- You want to preserve morphological features learned by the Phi layers while adapting the final predictions

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49]()

---

## The `model_fine_tune` Function

The primary interface for fine-tuning is the `model_fine_tune` function located in [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49]().

### Function Signature

```python
def model_fine_tune(model, dataloader, rho=False, gene_expression=True, max_epochs=10)
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `model` | `DeepCell` or `DeepSpot` | Required | The pre-trained model to fine-tune |
| `dataloader` | `DataLoader` | Required | PyTorch DataLoader containing the new training data |
| `rho` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, unfreeze and train the `rho` layers (final aggregation modules) |
| `gene_expression` | `bool` | `True` | If `True`, unfreeze and train the `gene_expression` layer |
| `max_epochs` | `int` | `10` | Number of epochs to train the unfrozen layers |

### Behavior

The function implements selective layer training by:

1. **Freezing all parameters** by setting `requires_grad=False` for all model parameters
2. **Selectively unfreezing** based on flags:
   - If `rho=True`: Unfreezes all parameters in `model.rho` modules
   - If `gene_expression=True`: Unfreezes all parameters in `model.gene_expression` layer
3. **Creating a filtered optimizer** that only updates trainable parameters using AdamW
4. **Setting training modes**: Model is set to `eval()` except for unfrozen layers which are set to `train()`
5. **Training via Lightning**: Uses `L.Trainer` with logging and checkpointing disabled

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49]()

---

## Fine-tuning Architecture

The following diagram illustrates which components can be fine-tuned in the DeepCell/DeepSpot architecture:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Layer"
        Input["Image Features<br/>(foundation model embeddings)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phi Layers (Feature Transformation)"
        PhiModules["phi_cell / phi_spot<br/>nn.ModuleList<br/>n=10 ensemble members"]
        PhiState["Status: FROZEN<br/>requires_grad=False"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rho Layers (Aggregation & Prediction)"
        RhoModules["model.rho<br/>nn.ModuleList<br/>n=10 ensemble members"]
        RhoState["Status: CONDITIONAL<br/>Unfrozen if rho=True"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Gene Expression Layer"
        GeneExpr["model.gene_expression<br/>(if present)"]
        GeneState["Status: CONDITIONAL<br/>Unfrozen if gene_expression=True"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Predictions["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    end
    
    Input --> PhiModules
    PhiModules -.->|frozen| PhiState
    PhiModules --> RhoModules
    RhoModules -.->|conditional| RhoState
    RhoModules --> GeneExpr
    GeneExpr -.->|conditional| GeneState
    GeneExpr --> Predictions
```

**Layer Freezing Strategy**: The Phi layers remain frozen during fine-tuning to preserve morphological feature extraction learned from the original dataset. The Rho layers and gene expression layer can be selectively unfrozen to adapt the final predictions to the new dataset's gene expression patterns.

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:125-127]()

---

## Fine-tuning Workflow

The following diagram shows the complete fine-tuning process from loading a pre-trained model to obtaining predictions on new data:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start: Pre-trained Model + New Dataset"]
    
    subgraph "Step 1: Load Pre-trained Model"
        LoadModel["Load model checkpoint<br/>DeepCell.load_from_checkpoint()<br/>or DeepSpot.load_from_checkpoint()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 2: Prepare Fine-tuning Data"
        PrepData["Create DataLoader<br/>DeepCellDataLoader or<br/>DeepSpotDataLoader<br/>with new dataset"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 3: Configure Fine-tuning"
        SetFlags["Set fine-tuning flags:<br/>rho=True/False<br/>gene_expression=True/False<br/>max_epochs=N"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 4: Execute Fine-tuning"
        CallFT["model_fine_tune(model, dataloader,<br/>rho=rho, gene_expression=gene_expr,<br/>max_epochs=max_epochs)"]
        Freeze["Freeze all parameters<br/>param.requires_grad = False"]
        Unfreeze["Unfreeze selected layers<br/>based on flags"]
        CreateOpt["Create AdamW optimizer<br/>for trainable params only"]
        SetModes["Set eval() + train()<br/>for unfrozen layers"]
        Train["L.Trainer.fit(model, dataloader)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Step 5: Save & Deploy"
        Save["Save fine-tuned model<br/>checkpoint"]
        Inference["Run inference on<br/>new samples"]
    end
    
    Start --> LoadModel
    LoadModel --> PrepData
    PrepData --> SetFlags
    SetFlags --> CallFT
    CallFT --> Freeze
    Freeze --> Unfreeze
    Unfreeze --> CreateOpt
    CreateOpt --> SetModes
    SetModes --> Train
    Train --> Save
    Save --> Inference
```

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49]()

---

## Code Example

Here is a typical fine-tuning workflow:

### Step 1: Load Pre-trained Model

```python
from deepspot.cell.model import DeepCell

# Load pre-trained model
model = DeepCell.load_from_checkpoint(
    "path/to/pretrained_checkpoint.ckpt",
    input_size=1024,
    output_size=500
)
```

### Step 2: Prepare Fine-tuning DataLoader

```python
from deepspot.cell.dataloader import DeepCellDataLoader

# Create dataloader with new dataset
finetune_loader = DeepCellDataLoader(
    adata=new_adata,
    image_features_path="path/to/new_features",
    batch_size=32,
    n_hops=1,
    neighbor_context=45,
    split_type="train"
)
```

### Step 3: Execute Fine-tuning

```python
from deepspot.utils.utils import model_fine_tune

# Fine-tune only the rho layers for 10 epochs
model_fine_tune(
    model=model,
    dataloader=finetune_loader,
    rho=True,
    gene_expression=False,
    max_epochs=10
)
```

### Step 4: Save Fine-tuned Model

```python
# Save the fine-tuned checkpoint
trainer.save_checkpoint("path/to/finetuned_checkpoint.ckpt")
```

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49]()

---

## Layer Selection Strategy

The choice of which layers to fine-tune depends on your use case:

| Scenario | `rho` | `gene_expression` | Rationale |
|----------|-------|-------------------|-----------|
| **New tissue type, similar morphology** | `True` | `True` | Adapt final predictions while keeping feature extraction |
| **Different gene panel** | `False` | `True` | Only adapt gene-specific output layer |
| **Same genes, different protocol** | `True` | `False` | Adapt aggregation but keep gene mappings |
| **Maximum adaptation** | `True` | `True` | Unfreeze all prediction layers |

### Rho Layers

The `rho` layers ([deepspot/cell/model.py:126-127]()) are ensemble modules that aggregate transformed features and produce intermediate representations. Unfreezing these layers allows the model to learn new aggregation patterns specific to your dataset.

```python
# Rho module structure (from DeepCell.__init__)
self.rho = nn.ModuleList([
    Rho(phi2rho_size * self._get_phi_multiplier(cell_context),
        output_size, self.p_rho) 
    for _ in range(self.n_ensemble_rho)
])
```

### Gene Expression Layer

The `gene_expression` layer is the final output layer that maps from the Rho output space to individual gene predictions. This layer is dataset-specific and typically should be fine-tuned when adapting to new data.

Sources: [deepspot/cell/model.py:126-127](), [deepspot/utils/utils.py:25-32]()

---

## Optimizer Configuration

During fine-tuning, the function creates a new optimizer that only operates on trainable parameters:

```python
# From model_fine_tune
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
    filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, model.parameters()),
    lr=model.hparams.lr, 
    weight_decay=model.hparams.weight_decay
)
```

This uses:
- **AdamW optimizer**: Same optimizer as used during initial training
- **Filtered parameters**: Only parameters with `requires_grad=True` are included
- **Inherited hyperparameters**: Learning rate and weight decay from the original model's `hparams`

The learning rate from the original model is reused, which is typically appropriate for fine-tuning. If you need a different learning rate, modify `model.hparams.lr` before calling `model_fine_tune`.

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:35-38]()

---

## Training Mode Management

The function carefully manages PyTorch training modes to ensure proper behavior:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Initial State"
        AllParams["All model parameters<br/>requires_grad=False"]
    end
    
    subgraph "After Selective Unfreezing"
        FrozenLayers["Phi layers<br/>mode: eval()"]
        UnfrozenRho["Rho layers (if enabled)<br/>mode: train()"]
        UnfrozenGene["Gene expression (if enabled)<br/>mode: train()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "During Training"
        Forward["Forward pass uses:<br/>- Frozen layers in eval mode (no dropout)<br/>- Unfrozen layers in train mode (with dropout)"]
        Backward["Backward pass updates:<br/>- Only unfrozen parameters<br/>- Frozen parameters unchanged"]
    end
    
    AllParams --> FrozenLayers
    AllParams --> UnfrozenRho
    AllParams --> UnfrozenGene
    
    FrozenLayers --> Forward
    UnfrozenRho --> Forward
    UnfrozenGene --> Forward
    
    Forward --> Backward
```

The dual-mode approach ensures:
1. **Frozen layers** use `eval()` mode to disable dropout and batch normalization updates
2. **Unfrozen layers** use `train()` mode to enable dropout for regularization
3. **Gradients** only flow through unfrozen layers during backpropagation

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:39-45]()

---

## Lightning Trainer Configuration

The fine-tuning process uses PyTorch Lightning's `Trainer` with specific configurations:

```python
trainer = L.Trainer(
    max_epochs=max_epochs, 
    logger=False, 
    enable_checkpointing=False
)
trainer.fit(model, dataloader)
```

### Configuration Details

| Parameter | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `max_epochs` | User-specified (default: 10) | Controls training duration |
| `logger` | `False` | Disables automatic logging (simplified fine-tuning) |
| `enable_checkpointing` | `False` | Disables automatic checkpoint saving |

This minimal configuration is designed for quick fine-tuning experiments. For production fine-tuning with logging and checkpointing, you may want to create your own `Trainer` instance instead of using the convenience function.

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:47-48]()

---

## Best Practices

### 1. Start with Fewer Epochs

Fine-tuning typically requires fewer epochs than training from scratch. Start with `max_epochs=5-10` and monitor for overfitting.

### 2. Validate on Hold-out Data

Since the convenience function doesn't provide validation monitoring, manually evaluate on a validation set:

```python
# Fine-tune on training data
model_fine_tune(model, train_loader, rho=True, max_epochs=10)

# Evaluate on validation data
from deepspot.utils.utils import run_inference_from_dataloader
val_predictions = run_inference_from_dataloader(model, val_loader, device="cuda")
```

### 3. Consider Layer Selection

- **Conservative approach**: Start with `gene_expression=True, rho=False` to minimize changes
- **Aggressive approach**: Use `gene_expression=True, rho=True` for maximum adaptation
- **Never unfreeze Phi**: The Phi layers contain morphological features that generalize well across datasets

### 4. Monitor for Overfitting

The DeepCell model tracks losses internally. After fine-tuning, visualize the training progression:

```python
model.plot_loss()  # Available from DeepCell.plot_loss()
```

### 5. Preserve Original Model

Always save your pre-trained model before fine-tuning, as the function modifies the model in-place:

```python
# Save original before fine-tuning
import torch
torch.save(model.state_dict(), "pretrained_backup.pth")

# Now fine-tune
model_fine_tune(model, dataloader, rho=True, max_epochs=10)
```

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49](), [deepspot/cell/model.py:235-281]()

---

## Limitations and Considerations

### Parameter Filtering

The function uses `filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, model.parameters())` to identify trainable parameters. This means:
- Only explicitly unfrozen parameters will be updated
- Any custom layers not covered by the `rho` or `gene_expression` flags will remain frozen
- If your model has additional custom layers, you'll need to unfreeze them manually

### No Validation Loop

The function trains without validation monitoring. For production use, consider implementing your own fine-tuning loop with:
- Validation data
- Early stopping based on validation loss
- Learning rate scheduling
- Checkpoint saving

### Fixed Learning Rate

The function reuses the learning rate from `model.hparams.lr`. For fine-tuning, you may want to use a lower learning rate (e.g., 10-100x smaller than the original training rate).

### Gene Expression Layer Dependency

The `gene_expression` flag assumes the model has a `model.gene_expression` attribute. Verify your model architecture includes this layer before setting `gene_expression=True`.

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49]()

---

## Relationship to Other Components

Fine-tuning integrates with several other DeepSpot components:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PretrainedWeights["Pre-trained Weights<br/>(Zenodo or local)"]
    ModelClass["DeepCell / DeepSpot<br/>LightningModule"]
    
    DataLoader["DeepCellDataLoader /<br/>DeepSpotDataLoader"]
    NewData["New Dataset<br/>(AnnData + features)"]
    
    FineTune["model_fine_tune()<br/>utils.utils"]
    
    TrainLoop["L.Trainer.fit()<br/>Lightning training"]
    
    Inference["run_inference_from_dataloader()<br/>or predict_*_from_image_path()"]
    
    SavedModel["Fine-tuned Checkpoint<br/>.ckpt file"]
    
    PretrainedWeights --> ModelClass
    NewData --> DataLoader
    ModelClass --> FineTune
    DataLoader --> FineTune
    FineTune --> TrainLoop
    TrainLoop --> SavedModel
    SavedModel --> Inference
```

**Integration Points:**
- **Input**: Requires a pre-trained model loaded via `DeepCell.load_from_checkpoint()` or `DeepSpot.load_from_checkpoint()`
- **Data**: Uses standard `DeepCellDataLoader` or `DeepSpotDataLoader` instances (see [#4.3](#4.3) and [#4.4](#4.4))
- **Output**: Produces a modified model that can be saved and used with standard inference functions (see [#6.3](#6.3))
- **Loss tracking**: Leverages the model's built-in `training_loss` and `validation_loss` attributes (see [deepspot/cell/model.py:121-122]())

Sources: [deepspot/utils/utils.py:20-49](), [deepspot/utils/utils.py:51-69]()
